get.summary: Get a state session law's text
get.description:
The act's text exactly as printed, one page of about 30,000 characters at a
time, cut at a paragraph break where one is near. Follow `nextCursor` while
`hasMore` is true; `pageStart` / `pageEnd` / `totalChars` are character offsets
into the whole text, and concatenating the pages in order reproduces it.

**Cost**: 6 credits per page served. Read `estimatedBodyPages` on the law first
(`charCount` divided by about 30,000). A short act is one page; an omnibus act can
be many. Each page is charged on its own, so you can stop whenever you have enough.
`pagePrice` is what this page cost, `totalPages` the estimated pages in all, and
`estimatedRemainingCredits` the pages still to come times the price.

**Cost of reading a law.** Reading a whole law is `estimatedBodyPages` times the price
of one body page (6 credits). Both are on the record: `charCount` is its length
in characters and `estimatedBodyPages` is that divided by the page size (about
30,000 characters), rounded up, and null unless the text is served. Most acts
take a page or two. The longest we hold, Ohio's 2025 budget act (HB 96, 9,571,132
characters), takes about 320 pages, 1,920 credits to read in
full, so check `estimatedBodyPages` before you page through an omnibus act. Each body
response then carries `pagePrice` (what that page cost) and `estimatedRemainingCredits`
(the pages still to come times the price) so you can stop whenever you have enough.

**Where a page starts.** Follow `nextCursor` from the page before, or send `startChar`,
a character offset into the text (0-based, the scale of `pageStart` and `totalChars`),
to jump straight to a place you know without paging from the start. Send one or the
other, never both (a 422, uncharged). A `startChar` page costs and sizes the same as any
other, and returns a normal signed `nextCursor`. `startChar` has no version binding of
its own, so add `expectTextSha256` (the `textSha256` you read the text under, in
lowercase hex, 16 characters or more): if the text was re-collected since, the answer is
a 409 and nothing is charged. A `startChar` at or beyond the end is a 422, refunded.
There is no page-size parameter: a page is always about 30,000 characters, so
its price is fixed.

**Attribution.** Every outcome carries `citation`, `jurisdiction`, `session`,
`approvedDate` and `sourceUrl`, so a page is attributable on its own. `sourceUrl` is the
official copy on a government host and is present when the text is withheld or not held,
so a reader always has somewhere to go.

**Id only.** This route takes a `sessionLawId`, not a citation: resolve a citation
once with `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}` and use the id it returns.

**Not served, not charged.** When we do not serve the text (`textStatus` is not
`held`), the answer is a 200 with `available: false` and a `reason` (`not_held`,
`withheld`, `pending` or `empty_text`), `creditsConsumed: 0`, the
`withheldReason` for a withheld law, and the official `sourceUrl`. A federal id (`SAL_...`) is a 404
(`federal_session_law`); read federal session laws with
`GET /us/statutes/section/{actId}`. An unknown id is a 404; a stale cursor or a mismatched `expectTextSha256` is a 409
(start again without `cursor`); a malformed or expired cursor, `cursor` with `startChar`,
or a `startChar` past the end is a 422. None of these is
charged, and a failure on our side (500, 503) is refunded.

**Amendatory markup.** An amending act prints the language it deletes and inserts.
Where `amendatoryMarkup` is `preserved`, that markup is in `text` in the convention
`markupConvention` names: `wdiff` writes deleted language `[-like this-]` and
inserted language `{+like this+}`; `publisher_literal` keeps the publisher's own
markers as printed (Minnesota's `new text begin` and `deleted text begin`); `mixed`
has both. Where it is `lost`, the publisher printed markup our text does not keep,
so deleted words can read as law: check the source before quoting. Only the as
printed text is served; there is no clean "as enacted" view.

**Example**

```bash
curl "https://api.vaquill.ai/api/v1/us/session-laws/SSL_MN_2025S1_G_Y2025_C1/body" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VAQUILL_API_KEY"

# jump to a character offset, pinned to the version of the text you read
curl "https://api.vaquill.ai/api/v1/us/session-laws/SSL_MN_2025S1_G_Y2025_C1/body?startChar=29987&expectTextSha256=02693d5b55d4709b" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VAQUILL_API_KEY"
```

```javascript
const MY_BUDGET = 100; // the most you will spend to finish reading, in credits
let cursor;
let text = "";
do {
  const url = new URL("https://api.vaquill.ai/api/v1/us/session-laws/SSL_MN_2025S1_G_Y2025_C1/body");
  if (cursor) url.searchParams.set("cursor", cursor);
  const res = await fetch(url, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.VAQUILL_API_KEY}` },
  });
  const page = await res.json();
  if (!page.available) break; // withheld or not held: page.sourceUrl is the official copy
  text += page.text;
  if (page.estimatedRemainingCredits > MY_BUDGET) break; // stop whenever you have enough
  cursor = page.nextCursor;
} while (cursor);
```

**Related endpoints**

- `GET /us/statutes/resolve` answers a citation that names a state session law
  rather than a code section with a `sessionLaw` block (`matched`, or `ambiguous`
  with every candidate), pointing here. It never changes `resolved` or `section`.
- `GET /us/statutes/coverage` lists, per jurisdiction under `sessionLaws`, which
  sessions we hold session laws for and whether each is `complete` or `partial`.
  Read it first: a law missing from a `partial` session is not evidence that it
  does not exist.
- Federal session laws (the Statutes at Large, `SAL_` ids) are not served here. Read
  them with `GET /us/statutes/section/{actId}`.

**Nulls.** Every field of a response is always present: one with no value is `null`
(or `[]` for a list). The examples on this page leave the nulls out for brevity. The
exceptions are blocks that exist only when they apply and are OMITTED otherwise, never
null: `publisher`, `provenance` and `session.coverageStatus` on a law, and `coverage` on a
list page that has rows.

**Rate limits.** Calls count against your key's per-minute budget like every Data
API route; a 429 carries `Retry-After`.

parameters.name: session_law_id

schema.description:
A STATE session law's id, for example `SSL_MN_2025S1_G_Y2025_C1`, from a `/us/session-laws/list` result.

A citation also works here on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`, and `resolvedFrom` says what your input matched. Name the state in the citation: `Minn. Laws 2025, ch. 1`, `2025 Minn. Laws ch. 1`, `Ch. 1, Laws of Minnesota 2025`, `Ch. 2025-12, Laws of Fla.`, `2025 Wash. Sess. Laws ch. 12`, `La. Acts 2025, No. 12`, `Pa. Act 12 of 2025`, `Minn. S.F. 1552 (2025)`, `MN: Laws 2025, ch. 1`. A form only one state uses needs no state: `P.A. 104-0001` (Illinois), `Pub. Act No. 26-151` (Connecticut), `S.L. 2025-12` (North Carolina), `Stats. 2025, ch. 12` (California), `D.C. Law 25-713`. The publisher's printed form (`CHAPTER 2025-12`, `S.F.No. 1552`) and the `citation` we print on every law also work. A form several states share (`Laws 2025, ch. 1`, `HB 123`, `Act 12 of 2025`) is a 404 with `reason: needs_jurisdiction`, the states it exists in and one candidate per state: we never guess the state. A citation naming several laws of one state (Minnesota 2025 has two Chapter 1s) is a 404 listing all of them, `candidateCount` and `truncated` saying whether the list is complete, and `defaultSessionLawId` the regular session's law where there is exactly one conventional reading. An id or citation that matches nothing in a session we have only partly collected is a 404 with `reason: session_not_fully_collected` and that session's coverage: the law may exist and not be held yet, so it is never charged, the resolve price included. A citation costs the route's price PLUS the `/us/statutes/resolve` price (2 credits), the second charged whether or not it resolves. URL-encode the citation; one containing `/` cannot travel in a path segment.

Federal session laws (`SAL_...`, `Pub. L. 118-5`, the Statutes at Large) are served by `/us/statutes/section`, not here, and code citations (`26 U.S.C. § 1`) by `/us/statutes/resolve`.

get.summary: Get a state session law, by id or by citation
get.description:
Everything we hold about one STATE session law except its text: identity and
citation, session, approval date, every printed effective date (`effectiveDates`,
always a list), other printed dates, the code sections the publisher's own table
lists the act as affecting (`codeSectionsAffected`), its sources with hashes, and
whether its text is held. Fetch the text itself, paged, from
`/us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`.

**Cost**: 2 credits. Pass a citation where the id goes and it adds the
`/us/statutes/resolve` price (2 credits), kept whether or not the citation
resolves, so `creditsConsumed` is then 4. A 404 never keeps this
route's own price; a failure on our side (500, 503) is refunded in full. A 422
is never charged.

**Id or citation.** Send a `sessionLawId` from a list result, or a citation or
bill number (`S.F.No. 1552`); the `sessionLawId` path parameter says which forms
are matched and how. `resolvedFrom` tells you what your input matched, and the
`sessionLawId` to send next time. A citation matching several laws is a 404 with
`reason: ambiguous_citation`, every candidate in `didYouMean`, and none chosen for you.
Prefer the id: it is free of the resolve fee and unambiguous. When a citation names no
state (`Laws 2025, ch. 1`), pass the optional `jurisdiction` (`mn`) to scope it: it
supplies the state, and it vetoes a conflicting one (`Minn. Laws 2025, ch. 1` with
`jurisdiction=tx` is a 404 `unresolved_citation`). It has no effect on an id.

**Citing and sourcing.** `citableAs` is the law in the form a lawyer writes
(`Minn. Laws 2025, ch. 1`), and `citationShort` a compact label for tables
(`MN ch. 1 (2025)`); either is null where we do not know the state's form, never a
guess, and `citableAs` resolves back to this law. `sourceUrl` is the official page
the text was collected from, on a government host, and is present on a withheld
law too. `licenseNote` says what the law's licence class permits.

**What the dates mean.** `approvedDate` is when the act was signed and is never an
effective date. Where the registry holds none but the publisher dates the governor's
signature among its other milestones (South Dakota's `Signed by the Governor`), we
fill it from that label and say so with `approvedDateDerived: true`; a presented or
passed date is never read as an approval, and a derived date is not matched by the
list's `approvedFrom` and `approvedTo`. `effectiveDates` holds the dates the publisher prints as effective
and is empty, not guessed, when none is printed or it is printed as a rule ("the
day following final enactment"); empty does not mean the act is not in force.
`otherDates` holds the rest (approval, filing, presentment) each with its `kind`.
`codeSectionsAffected` is the publisher's table as printed and is empty when the
publisher prints none, though `title` usually names the sections in prose.

**What the publisher printed.** `publisher` carries what the publisher itself
states about the act: `publisherFields`, its own structured fields verbatim (Texas gives the
bill's full action history with journal pages, Maryland the committees and reading dates,
North Carolina and New Mexico a history that can include vote counts, most states little
more than a bill number and a sponsor), plus `publisherIds`, `otherCitations`,
`legislatureNumber`, `sessionLastYear`, `printedPageStart` and `printedPageEnd` and the
label the document carries for its own kind (`documentKindAsPrinted`). The keys of
`publisherFields` differ by state and are the publisher's words, not ours: nothing is
normalised, and a key that is absent is not a fact about the act. `provenance` says how the
text was obtained (`textMethod`, `pagesWithText`, and the bound `volume` and pages it was
cut from) and lists the collector's own `caveats` on the record, verbatim: most say
something about the act or its text a reader should know, and some are working notes about
how the record was assembled. `session.coverageStatus` says whether we hold the whole
session (`complete`) or only part of it (`partial`, so a missing neighbour may exist).
These three are omitted, not null, if they cannot be read; the rest of the answer and its
price are the same.

**Withheld text.** A law whose text has a measured defect is still returned in
full, with `textStatus: withheld` and the `withheldReason`; only its text is held
back (`/body` answers `available: false`, free). Check `amendatoryMarkup` before
quoting an amending act: where it is `lost`, deleted words can read as law.

**Cost of reading a law.** Reading a whole law is `estimatedBodyPages` times the price
of one body page (6 credits). Both are on the record: `charCount` is its length
in characters and `estimatedBodyPages` is that divided by the page size (about
30,000 characters), rounded up, and null unless the text is served. Most acts
take a page or two. The longest we hold, Ohio's 2025 budget act (HB 96, 9,571,132
characters), takes about 320 pages, 1,920 credits to read in
full, so check `estimatedBodyPages` before you page through an omnibus act. Each body
response then carries `pagePrice` (what that page cost) and `estimatedRemainingCredits`
(the pages still to come times the price) so you can stop whenever you have enough.

**Example**

```bash
curl "https://api.vaquill.ai/api/v1/us/session-laws/SSL_MN_2025R_G_Y2025_C1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VAQUILL_API_KEY"

# the same law by bill number (URL-encode the citation)
curl "https://api.vaquill.ai/api/v1/us/session-laws/S.F.No.%201552" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VAQUILL_API_KEY"

# a citation that names no state, scoped to one
curl "https://api.vaquill.ai/api/v1/us/session-laws/Laws%202025,%20ch.%201?jurisdiction=mn" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VAQUILL_API_KEY"
```

```javascript
const id = "SSL_MN_2025R_G_Y2025_C1";
const res = await fetch(`https://api.vaquill.ai/api/v1/us/session-laws/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`, {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.VAQUILL_API_KEY}` },
});
const law = await res.json();
```

**Related endpoints**

- `GET /us/statutes/resolve` answers a citation that names a state session law
  rather than a code section with a `sessionLaw` block (`matched`, or `ambiguous`
  with every candidate), pointing here. It never changes `resolved` or `section`.
- `GET /us/statutes/coverage` lists, per jurisdiction under `sessionLaws`, which
  sessions we hold session laws for and whether each is `complete` or `partial`.
  Read it first: a law missing from a `partial` session is not evidence that it
  does not exist.
- Federal session laws (the Statutes at Large, `SAL_` ids) are not served here. Read
  them with `GET /us/statutes/section/{actId}`.

**Nulls.** Every field of a response is always present: one with no value is `null`
(or `[]` for a list). The examples on this page leave the nulls out for brevity. The
exceptions are blocks that exist only when they apply and are OMITTED otherwise, never
null: `publisher`, `provenance` and `session.coverageStatus` on a law, and `coverage` on a
list page that has rows.

**Rate limits.** Calls count against your key's per-minute budget like every Data
API route; a 429 carries `Retry-After`.

schema.description:
A STATE session law's id, for example `SSL_MN_2025S1_G_Y2025_C1`, from a `/us/session-laws/list` result.

A citation also works here on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`, and `resolvedFrom` says what your input matched. Name the state in the citation: `Minn. Laws 2025, ch. 1`, `2025 Minn. Laws ch. 1`, `Ch. 1, Laws of Minnesota 2025`, `Ch. 2025-12, Laws of Fla.`, `2025 Wash. Sess. Laws ch. 12`, `La. Acts 2025, No. 12`, `Pa. Act 12 of 2025`, `Minn. S.F. 1552 (2025)`, `MN: Laws 2025, ch. 1`. A form only one state uses needs no state: `P.A. 104-0001` (Illinois), `Pub. Act No. 26-151` (Connecticut), `S.L. 2025-12` (North Carolina), `Stats. 2025, ch. 12` (California), `D.C. Law 25-713`. The publisher's printed form (`CHAPTER 2025-12`, `S.F.No. 1552`) and the `citation` we print on every law also work. A form several states share (`Laws 2025, ch. 1`, `HB 123`, `Act 12 of 2025`) is a 404 with `reason: needs_jurisdiction`, the states it exists in and one candidate per state: we never guess the state. An id or citation that matches nothing in a session we have only partly collected is a 404 with `reason: session_not_fully_collected` and that session's coverage: the law may exist and not be held yet, so it is never charged, the resolve price included. A citation costs the route's price PLUS the `/us/statutes/resolve` price (2 credits), the second charged whether or not it resolves. URL-encode the citation; one containing `/` cannot travel in a path segment.

Federal session laws (`SAL_...`, `Pub. L. 118-5`, the Statutes at Large) are served by `/us/statutes/section`, not here, and code citations (`26 U.S.C. § 1`) by `/us/statutes/resolve`.

Every error (400/401/402/403/404/405/422/429/5xx) carries a `detail`

the API. A 422 adds `errors`, one entry per rejected field. Some 404s add

engine.title: Engine
engine.description:
WHICH BACKEND ANSWERED. `asOf` is one parameter over two engines and they make different promises.

`stored_edition`: the answer is a publisher's own printed edition of the text, held verbatim. Used wherever we hold published editions, which today is `corpusType=CFR_ANNUAL` (annual editions per title), the US Code, the Copyright Compendium and OFAC FAQs. The date is resolved to a held edition and that edition's text is returned as printed.

Coverage under this engine is per corpus and is NOT continuous. The CFR annual editions tile the calendar per title; the others are ENUMERATED editions with gaps between them. A date that falls in a gap returns `source: "unavailable"` with `outOfCoverageReason` and NO text, rather than the neighbouring edition, because the text may have changed in the gap. For the US Code in particular, most dates are currently out of coverage: see `outOfCoverageReason` for which editions we hold.

`observed_change`: the answer is RECONSTRUCTED from changes we observed, and reaches back only as far as capture began for that source. Every other corpus.

Read this before `isBounded`, which does not make the same claim on both engines.

source.title: Source
source.description:
The detail WITHIN the engine above.

On `observed_change` -- `live`: we captured no change to this section after your date, so today's text is what stood then as far as we ever saw. `reconstructed`: rebuilt from the before-side of the first change we captured after your date. `unavailable`: we know it changed but cannot rebuild the earlier text, so no text is returned. That is different from the section being empty, and different again from it not existing.

On `stored_edition` -- `published`: an edition we hold answered, verbatim. `unavailable`: the date is out of coverage for this section and no text is returned, and `outOfCoverageReason` says why in a sentence. Out of coverage means the date falls outside every edition we hold, or inside a gap between two of them; it is never answered from a neighbouring edition.

existed.title: Existed
existed.description: False when the earliest thing we ever captured for this section is its ADDITION and that addition postdates your date, so it demonstrably did not exist yet. A real answer, not a miss.

basisChangeId.title: Basischangeid
basisChangeId.description: The change event whose before-side supplied this text. Null when `source` is `live`. Pass it to `/us/statutes/section/{actId}/changes` to see the event this answer rests on.

observedFrom.title: Observedfrom
observedFrom.description: The earliest change we ever captured for this section. Null when we captured none. This is how far back the reconstruction can see, and it is a property of when capture began for this source, not of the age of the law.

resolvedEditionYear.title: Resolvededitionyear
resolvedEditionYear.description: `stored_edition` only. The revision year actually served, read from the edition's own printed revision statement. 🔴 This is NOT always the year the schedule computes: a publisher reprints an unchanged volume into the next year without re-dating it, so the 2024 printing of 4 CFR is the January 1 2019 revision. Render THIS year, never `scheduledEditionYear`.

scheduledEditionYear.title: Schedulededitionyear
scheduledEditionYear.description: `stored_edition` only. The edition the revision schedule says SHOULD cover your date. Differs from `resolvedEditionYear` whenever the publisher reprinted an unchanged volume. Exposed so the disagreement is auditable, not so it can be displayed.

editionsObserved.title: Editionsobserved
editionsObserved.description: `stored_edition` only. Every edition year in which this exact text was observed, enumerated. An ENUMERATION, not a range: a year between the first and last that is absent here is an edition nobody read, and a date resolving to it is reported out of coverage rather than answered from a neighbour.

outOfCoverageReason.title: Outofcoveragereason
outOfCoverageReason.description: Why no text was returned, in a sentence safe to show a reader. Null when text was returned.

isBounded.title: Isbounded
isBounded.description:
⚠️ This flag does NOT make the same claim on both engines. Read `engine` first.

On `stored_edition`, TRUE means your date falls inside the editions we actually parsed for this title, so the text is a verified published printing rather than an inference. FALSE means out of coverage, and no text is returned.

On `observed_change`, TRUE means: we observed no change affecting your date, and that is NOT the same as there having been none.

Set when your date predates `observedFrom`, or when we captured no change for this section at all. Change capture began long after the corpus did and is per-source, so a bounded answer is our best reconstruction rather than a verified historical text. Surface it. Rendering a bounded answer as authoritative point-in-time law makes a claim we did not make.

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: Prose statement of the same limit, safe to show a reader verbatim.

AsOfProvenance.title: AsOfProvenance
AsOfProvenance.description:
Where an `asOf` body came from, and how far the evidence reaches.

Every field but `text` on the parent exists so this answer cannot be
over-read. The corpus holds ONE current text per citation; an earlier one is
RECONSTRUCTED from observed changes, and observation started when it started.

figureId.title: Figureid
figureId.description: Stable id for this figure, also carried on the `<figure data-figure-id>` element in `html`. Deterministic, so it does not change between renders of the same source.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: What the image is. `equation` renders inline in the text.

caption.title: Caption
caption.description: The publisher's caption, when it prints one.

url.title: Url
url.description: Where the image is hosted, always on `statutes-us.vaquill.ai`. A format a browser cannot display (TIFF, EPS, PDF) is served as a PNG. Null when `status` is `unavailable`.

sourceUrl.title: Sourceurl
sourceUrl.description: The image as the government publisher serves it. Use it for a "view at source" link, especially when `status` is `unavailable`. Null when we hold no publishable link.

width.title: Width
width.description: Pixel width of the hosted image.

height.title: Height
height.description: Pixel height of the hosted image.

offsetMarkdown.title: Offsetmarkdown
offsetMarkdown.description: Character offset of this figure's placeholder in `markdown`, so a client can splice the image into its own layout.

offsetPlain.title: Offsetplain
offsetPlain.description: Character offset of this figure's `[Figure N: ...]` placeholder in `plain`.

status.title: Status
status.description: `unavailable` means the publisher's image could not be fetched. The figure is still listed, and its caption and placeholder stay in the text, so a missing figure is never silently dropped.

BodyFigure.title: BodyFigure
BodyFigure.description: One figure, equation or form image inside a rendered section body.

caption.title: Caption
caption.description: The table's caption, when it has one.

BodyTable.title: BodyTable
BodyTable.description: One table inside a rendered section body.

actId.title: Actid
actId.description: The section the citation names. Pass it to `/section/{actId}` to read it.

citation.title: Citation
citation.description: That section's citation, as it appears in results.

title.title: Title
examples: Civil action for deprivation of rights

state.title: State
state.description: That section's jurisdiction: `federal` or a two-letter state code.

excludedBy.title: Excludedby
excludedBy.description: The request filters that exclude the section, by their public names (`state`, `corpusType`, `code`, `article`, `titleNumber`, `chapter`, `part`, `yearFrom`, `yearTo`). Empty when the exclusion comes from a condition only the index can attribute (`excludeRepealed`, `actStatus`, `source`, `changedSince` and the Federal Register facets): then any of the filters you set may be responsible.

CitationOutsideFilters.title: CitationOutsideFilters
CitationOutsideFilters.description:
A citation that names a real section the caller's own filters exclude.

Both `/search` and `/resolve` treat a filter as a promise: a citation outside
it is not forced into the results. This says so, instead of leaving a caller
to read an unrelated top hit (or `resolved: false`) as "no such section".

sectionAsPrinted.title: Sectionasprinted
sectionAsPrinted.description: The code section the act changes, as the publisher's table prints it. Not normalised and not linked to an `actId` on `/us/statutes`.

actionAsPrinted.title: Actionasprinted
actionAsPrinted.description: What the act does to that section, in the publisher's own words or abbreviation (`AMD` amended, `ADD`, `REP`, ...).

codeAsPrinted.title: Codeasprinted
codeAsPrinted.description: The code the section belongs to, as printed.

actSectionAsPrinted.title: Actsectionasprinted
actSectionAsPrinted.description: The section of the act itself that makes the change.

CodeSectionAffected.title: CodeSectionAffected
CodeSectionAffected.description: A code section the publisher lists the act as affecting.

corpusType.title: Corpustype
corpusType.description: Board's corpus_type (e.g. `state`, `state_regulation`, `federal_register`, `agency_guidance`). Matched case-insensitively, so the uppercase spelling the statutes endpoints use for the same body of law (`USC`, `CFR`) works here too. Call GET /boards for the authoritative, current list -- corpus_type is a growing set as new corpora are added, not a fixed enum, and not every corpus we serve is a watchable board.

state.title: State
state.description: Board's state (2-letter, case-insensitive). For a federal board (USC, eCFR, the Federal Register) pass `federal` or omit this entirely; the two are equivalent. Must otherwise match the `state` GET /boards returned for this corpusType -- `GET /boards?corpusType=<type>` lists exactly those.

webhookUrl.title: Webhookurl
webhookUrl.description: Required when channel is webhook or both.

webhookSecret.title: Webhooksecret
webhookSecret.description: Optional signing secret, stored encrypted and never returned. When set, every delivery carries an `X-Vaquill-Signature: sha256=<hex>` header: HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body bytes, keyed with this secret. To verify, compute the same HMAC over the raw body you received (before parsing JSON) and compare it, constant-time, to the hex digest after `sha256=`.

emailAddress.title: Emailaddress
emailAddress.description: Required when channel is email or both.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description:
Optional narrowing so this alert covers one citation instead of an entire source. Four mutually exclusive forms.

**Hierarchy prefix** -- keys `title`, `chapter`, `part`, `section`, e.g. `{"title": "21", "part": "314"}` for 21 CFR part 314. Every level you set must match, so each one narrows further. `title` is required whenever any narrower level is set, and `section` also needs `chapter` or `part`: a bare part number matches across unrelated titles. Only sources whose documents carry a title/chapter/part hierarchy accept this form; the rest return 400.

**Exact section** -- `{"actId": "CFR_T21_P314_S314_50"}`, using the `actId` returned by search results and change events. Case-sensitive, and validated at create time against the corpus: an act_id we do not hold, or one belonging to a different source, is a 400 rather than a watch that could never fire. This form works on EVERY source, including flat ones with no hierarchy, so it is the only way to follow a single Federal Register document.

**Named source** -- `{"source": "fdic_fil"}`, for the corpora that fold several independent bodies of law behind one `corpusType`. The `agency_guidance` board alone carries 47 named sources across 24 agencies, so an unscoped watch on it delivers FDIC letters, IRS notices, OFAC FAQs and DOE appliance standards together. Accepted on `agency_adjudication`, `agency_guidance`, `agency_manuals`, `cfr`, `federal_rules`; anything else returns 400. The pickable values for a given board are on that board's `sources` array in `GET /boards` -- deliberately narrower than the `source` filter published on `POST /us/statutes/search`, because `agency_guidance` and `agency_manuals` are two boards reading one `corpusType` and each emits only its own half.

**Publishing agency** -- `{"agency": "irs"}`, covering every source that agency issues on the board. `source` is the unit we ingest and it is finer than the unit most callers think in: the IRS alone publishes 5 named series, so following it by source means one watch per series and a gap if you miss one. An agency scope is expanded WHEN AN EVENT IS MATCHED rather than when the watch is created, so a source registered after your watch is covered by it automatically, with no action from you. Accepted on `agency_adjudication`, `agency_guidance`, `agency_manuals`; the pickable values are on that board's `agencies` array in `GET /boards`.

Omit entirely to watch the whole source, which is the default and the pre-existing behavior.

webhookAuth.description: Optional outbound credential sent on every delivery, so your gateway can authenticate us with the header it already reads. Independent of `webhookSecret`: set neither, either, or both. Only valid on a webhook or both channel watch.

at.title: At
at.description: UTC instant at which the next credits expire.

credits.title: Credits
credits.description: Credits that expire at that instant. They stop being spendable immediately at `at`, not when the nightly sweep records it.

CreditExpiry.title: CreditExpiry
CreditExpiry.description: The soonest expiry, and what dies with it.

perMinute.title: Perminute
perMinute.description: Requests allowed per minute on this key, plan multiplier already applied.

perHour.title: Perhour
perHour.description: Requests allowed per hour on this key.

perDay.title: Perday
perDay.description: Requests allowed per day on this key.

CreditRateLimit.title: CreditRateLimit
CreditRateLimit.description:
Request-rate ceilings in force for the calling key.

A SECOND, independent ceiling alongside credits, and the two are unrelated:
you can hold credits and still be throttled, or sit far under these limits
and be refused for an empty balance.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the credits came from. `bonus` (signup grant), `subscription` (plan allowance, use-it-or-lose-it), `payg` (purchased packs) and `comp` (complimentary) exist today, and this list is not closed: read the values rather than matching on a fixed set.

credits.title: Credits
credits.description: Credits remaining in this source. 1 credit = $0.01.

CreditSourceBreakdown.title: CreditSourceBreakdown
CreditSourceBreakdown.description: Live credits held under one funding source.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Lowercase two-letter code of the section's jurisdiction. Null for a section that is not a state statute (a federal section).

sessionsHeld.title: Sessionsheld
sessionsHeld.description: The sessions of this jurisdiction whose code-section tables are held. A session not listed contributes nothing to `enactments`: an empty list says we read nothing, not that the section was untouched. Empty for an unsupported jurisdiction.

note.title: Note
note.description: In words: where the list comes from for this jurisdiction, and what it does not read. Show it beside the list: `enactments` is what the publisher's table prints, never a complete amendment history.
examples: Mississippi: the Legislature's bill-status record lists Code sections in a zero-padded form. Entries the publisher prints as a list or range are not matched.

EnactmentCoverage.title: EnactmentCoverage
EnactmentCoverage.description: What this answer is read from, and what it is not.

label.title: Label
label.description: The session's canonical label, as the publisher names it.

status.title: Status
status.description: Whether we hold every act of the session (`complete`) or only part of it (`partial`): an act missing from a partial session is not evidence that it did not touch the section. Null when coverage could not be read just now.

EnactmentSession.title: EnactmentSession
EnactmentSession.description: One legislative session of the jurisdiction whose code-section tables are read.

creditsRemaining.title: Creditsremaining
creditsRemaining.description:
Credits you can actually spend right now. Deliberately the same field name that metered responses return, so one name means one thing across the API.

Derived from your live credit buckets under the same expiry rule the billing path applies, so it never promises credits a call would refuse to spend.

usdRemaining.title: Usdremaining
usdRemaining.description: `creditsRemaining` in USD, at the published conversion rate (1 credit = $0.01). Provided so you do not have to hardcode the rate; `GET /api/v1/api-credits/pricing` is its source of truth.

bySource.title: Bysource
bySource.description: `creditsRemaining` split by funding source, and it always sums to it. Worth reading because the sources do not behave alike: `subscription` credits are use-it-or-lose-it at the period end, while `payg` credits you bought are durable and burn last.

nextExpiry.description: The soonest expiry across your credits, or `null` if none of them expire. Poll this to avoid silently forfeiting an allowance.

plan.title: Plan
plan.description: Active API subscription tier, or `null` on pay-as-you-go. Also determines your rate-limit multiplier. Briefly cached, so a subscription change made seconds ago may not be reflected yet; `creditsRemaining` is always live.

totalPurchased.title: Totalpurchased
totalPurchased.description: Lifetime credits added to this account.

totalConsumed.title: Totalconsumed
totalConsumed.description: Lifetime credits spent by this account.

rateLimit.description:
How fast this key may call, as opposed to how much it may spend. The two ceilings are independent: holding credits does not exempt you from these, and staying under these does not pay for a call.

These are the ceilings themselves, with your plan already applied, so you can size a client BEFORE issuing a request. The `X-RateLimit-*` headers on every response report the same ceilings plus your live headroom, and the two agree.

asOf.title: Asof
asOf.description: When this balance was computed. The value is live, not cached, so this is the instant the buckets were read.

ExternalCreditBalanceResponse.title: ExternalCreditBalanceResponse
ExternalCreditBalanceResponse.description: Spendable credit balance for the calling API key's account.

title.title: Title
title.description: The related document's own title/heading, when known.

documentType.title: Documenttype
documentType.description: `proposed_rule`, `final_rule`, or the raw Federal Register category otherwise.

publicationDate.title: Publicationdate
publicationDate.description: Federal Register publication date (ISO 8601 date), when known.

FrRelatedDocument.title: FrRelatedDocument
FrRelatedDocument.description:
One other Federal Register document sharing a RIN with this one.

A Regulation Identifier Number (RIN) tracks one regulatory action through
its lifecycle -- a proposed rule, its final rule, and any later
corrections all carry the same RIN. This is what answers "what happened
to this proposed rule": look up its RIN's other documents.

sessionLawId.title: Sessionlawid
sessionLawId.description: The act, in the session-law registry. Read it at `href`.

href.title: Href
href.description: Path of the act on this API: `GET` it for the record, or its `/body` for the text.

citation.title: Citation
citation.description: The act's citation as its publisher prints it. Null when none is held.

title.title: Title
title.description: The act's title as printed. Null when none is held.
examples: AN ACT TO AUTHORIZE A PERSON WHO IS THE HOLDER OF A WINE MANUFACTURER'S PERMIT

sessionCode.title: Sessioncode
sessionCode.description: The session the act was enacted in, as in `coverage.sessionsHeld`.

approvedDate.title: Approveddate
approvedDate.description: Date the governor approved the act, ISO 8601: never an effective date. Null when none is held.

effectiveDates.title: Effectivedates
effectiveDates.description: Every effective date the publisher prints for the ACT, in printed order: the act's, not necessarily this section's (an act can take effect in parts, and a date may carry a `scopeAsPrinted`). Empty when none is held, which does not mean the act is not in force.

action.title: Action
action.description: What the act did to the section, normalised: `added`, `amended`, `repealed`, `renumbered`, or `other`. It is mapped from `actionAsPrinted` only where the publisher's legend is settled; `other` means the table prints no action (Nebraska, `actionAsPrinted` is null), prints one that is not a change to this section (Mississippi's `BF`, brought forward), or one we do not map. Never read `other` as 'unchanged'. The publisher's own code is always in `actionAsPrinted`.

actionAsPrinted.title: Actionasprinted
actionAsPrinted.description: The publisher's own action code or word for this entry, verbatim. Null when the table prints none.

sectionAsPrinted.title: Sectionasprinted
sectionAsPrinted.description: The section exactly as the publisher's table prints it.

codeAsPrinted.title: Codeasprinted
codeAsPrinted.description: The code the publisher qualifies the section with, as printed (`HRS`, `D.C. Code`, `Education Code`). Null where the publisher prints none.

actSectionAsPrinted.title: Actsectionasprinted
actSectionAsPrinted.description: Which section of the ACT does it, as printed (Washington's `1223`, Kentucky's `5`). Null where the table prints none.

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: Where the entry comes from: always `publisher_sections_affected`, the publisher's own table of the code sections an act affects. Never read out of the act's prose.

matchQuality.title: Matchquality
matchQuality.description: How the entry was matched to the section: always `as_printed`, the publisher's printed section equals this section's number after folding case, spacing, dashes and the section sign, and nothing is matched by prefix. The match is on the number, in the jurisdiction's own printed form; it is not a legal analysis of what the act did.

identityConfidence.title: Identityconfidence
identityConfidence.description: How firmly the registry knows the act is the law it says it is: `confirmed`, `single_source`, `inferred` or `disputed`.

textStatus.title: Textstatus
textStatus.description: Whether we serve the act's text: `held`, `withheld`, `not_held` or `pending`, as on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

enactmentOutcome.title: Enactmentoutcome
enactmentOutcome.description: How the act became (or did not become) law, as on the act's record: `signed`, `vetoed` and so on. Null when it is not recorded.

SectionEnactment.title: SectionEnactment
SectionEnactment.description: One printed entry of a publisher's table: this act, against this section.

actId.title: Actid
actId.description: The section's act_id as served, after any citation or copy damage was resolved.

resolvedFrom.description: Present only when your input was a citation or an id carrying copy damage: what it was matched as. Null when you sent an exact act_id.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Lowercase two-letter code of the section's jurisdiction. Null for a federal section.

supported.title: Supported
supported.description: True when this section's jurisdiction is one whose publisher table is mapped to the statutes section numbers and this section is in the form that mapping was proven on: then `enactments` is an answer, even when it is empty, and the call is charged. False when it is not (see `reason`): `enactments` is empty, says nothing about the section, and the call is NOT charged.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why `supported` is false. `unsupported_jurisdiction`: we do not read this jurisdiction's table (none is printed, or its form is not verified against our section numbers), see `coverage.note`. `not_a_state_code_section`: the section is not a state statute (a federal, regulation or constitution section). `section_not_in_proven_form`: the jurisdiction is read, but this section's stored number is not in a form the mapping was proven on, so it is not guessed at. Null when `supported` is true.

enactments.title: Enactments
enactments.description: The entries of the publisher's tables whose printed section is this section, newest act first (by approval date, undated last), one per printed entry: an act that lists the section twice appears twice. NEVER a complete history: only acts we hold, in sessions we hold, whose table lists the section in the printed form this jurisdiction's mapping reads. Empty with `supported: true` is a real answer: no held table lists it.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: True when more entries matched than are returned (the newest are kept). A section amended by that many acts is not a case we have met.

coverage.description: What this answer is read from, and what it is not. Show it with the list.

creditsConsumed.title: Creditsconsumed
creditsConsumed.description: Credits actually charged for this call, never the list price. 0 when `supported` is false (refunded) and on a failure. A citation sent in place of the act_id adds the `/us/statutes/resolve` price, charged whether or not it resolves.

processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems
processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Not billed on.

input.title: Input
input.description: The identifier exactly as you sent it.

actId.title: Actid
actId.description: The act_id it matched. Send this next time to skip resolution.

via.title: Via
via.description: `citation` -- your input was a citation, resolved with the same resolver as `GET /us/statutes/resolve`. Check it the way you would check a `/resolve` answer. `normalized_id` -- your input was an act_id carrying surrounding whitespace, quotes, a trailing period or double percent-encoding, which were removed.

subsection.title: Subsection
subsection.description: The pincite your citation carried, e.g. `(h)(11)` for `26 U.S.C. § 1(h)(11)`. The WHOLE section is served; use `structured=true` on `/body` to address the subsection.

SectionIdentifierResolution.title: SectionIdentifierResolution
SectionIdentifierResolution.description:
How the identifier you sent was matched, when it was not an exact act_id.

Present only when the input did NOT match as sent. Absent (null) means the
section is exactly the act_id in your request.

sessionLawId.title: Sessionlawid
sessionLawId.description: Permanent identifier of the law, the key to use everywhere. Shape `SSL_{state}_{session code}_{series}[_Y{numberingYear}]_{C<chapter>|B<billKey>}`. It never changes: a correction to our reading of a law keeps the old id working. Pass it to `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

lawId.title: Lawid
lawId.description: The law's identifier in the open us1 scheme. Null until its identity is confirmed by a second source and the us1 state shape is minted, so it is null on every state law today. Use `sessionLawId`, which is always present.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Lowercase two-letter code of the state, `dc` or `pr`. Federal acts are not served by this family: they are on `/us/statutes/section`.

citation.title: Citation
citation.description: The act's citation as its publisher prints it, falling back to `{session label}, ch. {number}` when none is printed. It is NOT unique: many states print a bare `CHAPTER 1` every session. Key on `sessionLawId`.

citableAs.title: Citableas
citableAs.description: The law cited the way a lawyer writes it, from the state's own form: `Minn. Laws 2025, ch. 1`, `2025 Fla. Laws ch. 3`, `Ill. Pub. Act 104-0001`, `S.L. 2025-12` (North Carolina), `Stats. 2025, ch. 12` (California), `Ohio S.B. 1 (2025)` for a state that numbers no chapters. A law in a special or extraordinary session carries it (`Minn. Laws 2025, 1st Spec. Sess., ch. 1`). Every value is read back through the grammar that `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}` accepts a citation in, and must name this law; one that would not is null, never guessed. Null where the state's form is not known, for a series with no standard form (resolutions, memorials), or for a law with neither a chapter nor a bill key. Where a regular and a special session each have a chapter 1, the bare form is the regular session's law and resolves with that law flagged as the default; the special session's carries its session. Distinct from `citation`, which is the publisher's printed form.

citationShort.title: Citationshort
citationShort.description: A compact label for tables and badges: `MN ch. 1 (2025)`, `IL P.A. 104-0001`, `OH S.B. 1 (2025)`. Not a form to send back: use `citableAs` or the `sessionLawId`. Null exactly when `citableAs` is null.

session.description: The legislative session the law was enacted in, and whether we hold all of it (`coverageStatus`).

series.title: Series
series.description: The numbering series the law belongs to within its session. Most states have one, `general`. Others number acts, resolutions or local laws separately (`public`, `act`, `acts`, `law`, `public_act`, `resolve`, `resolution_chapter`, `local`, ...). An open list that grows as jurisdictions load. Filter with `series` on the list.

instrumentType.title: Instrumenttype
instrumentType.description: What kind of measure this is: `act`, `joint_resolution`, `concurrent_resolution`, `resolution`, `resolve`, `memorial` or `other`. An open list. A resolution that was numbered and published among the session laws is included, with `isLaw` saying whether it binds as law.

number.title: Number
number.description: The chapter or act number exactly as printed, as a string. It is not always an integer: `1`, `2025-12` (Florida), `104-0001` (Illinois), `1A`. Null where the state does not number its acts (see `billKey`).

billKey.title: Billkey
billKey.description: Normalised bill identifier (chamber and type letters plus the number) that stands in for a chapter number in states that do not number their acts (Missouri, Ohio, Nebraska). `House Bill 2` is `HB2`. Null whenever `number` is set. Part of the `sessionLawId` as `B<billKey>`.

billNumber.title: Billnumber
billNumber.description: The bill the act originated as, as the publisher prints it. Matches as a citation on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

numberingYear.title: Numberingyear
numberingYear.description: The year of the numbering sequence the chapter number belongs to, where the state numbers by year (Minnesota, Florida, Texas). It appears in the `sessionLawId` as `_Y2025`. A chapter number is only unique within a session and numbering year: Minnesota's regular and first special sessions of 2025 each have a Chapter 1. Null where one sequence runs across the session (Louisiana).

title.title: Title
title.description: The act's long title as printed, usually beginning `An act relating to`. It names the code sections the act amends in prose.
examples: An act relating to agriculture; modifying financial reporting requirements for grain buyers; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 223.17, subdivision 6.

shortTitle.title: Shorttitle
shortTitle.description: The act's short title when the publisher gives one (Ohio, New York, the District of Columbia and a few others do), otherwise null.
examples: Enact Advance Ohio Higher Education Act

approvedDate.title: Approveddate
approvedDate.description: Date the governor (or the equivalent authority) approved the act, ISO 8601. Never an effective date: an act is usually in force on a different day, which is `effectiveDates`. Null when the publisher prints no approval date. Where the registry holds none but the publisher's own dated label on `otherDates` names the governor's signature, it is filled from that label and `approvedDateDerived` is true. The `approvedFrom` and `approvedTo` filters do NOT match a derived date: they read the registry's own approval date.

approvedDateDerived.title: Approveddatederived
approvedDateDerived.description: True only when `approvedDate` was not held as an approval date and we filled it from a dated label printed on the act (today South Dakota's `Signed by the Governor`, listed under `otherDates`), on an act whose `enactmentOutcome` is `signed` or `line_item_veto`. False when `approvedDate` is null or is the registry's own. We never read a `presented` or `passed` date as an approval, nor a signing label on an act that became law without signature.

effectiveFirst.title: Effectivefirst
effectiveFirst.description: Earliest of the act's effective dates we hold. Null when we hold none: a date the publisher does not print, or prints as a relative rule (`the day following final enactment`), is not guessed. The full list is `effectiveDates` on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

effectiveLast.title: Effectivelast
effectiveLast.description: Latest of the act's effective dates we hold. Equal to `effectiveFirst` for an act with one date; null when we hold none.

enactmentOutcome.title: Enactmentoutcome
enactmentOutcome.description: How the measure became, or failed to become, law. `signed`; `became_law_without_signature`; `veto_overridden`; `line_item_veto` (signed with some items vetoed); `vetoed` and `pocket_veto` (not law); `not_presented` (no governor action recorded, usual for resolutions); `approved_by_voters`; `unknown` (the publisher does not say).

isLaw.title: Islaw
isLaw.description: True for an act that is law. False for a numbered measure that is not: a vetoed bill, a pocket veto. Null when `enactmentOutcome` does not settle it (`not_presented`, `unknown`).

textStatus.title: Textstatus
textStatus.description: Whether we serve this law's text. `held`: the text is served by `/us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`. `withheld`: we hold the text but a measured defect keeps it from being served, and `withheldReason` says what. `not_held`: we know the act exists and do not hold its text. `pending`: collected and not yet verified.

withheldReason.title: Withheldreason
withheldReason.description: Present only when `textStatus` is `withheld`: a plain sentence saying what is wrong with the text we hold and what would release it. Free text, not an enum: show it, do not branch on it. The record itself (dates, sources, title) is still served and still correct.
examples: LA: struck (deleted) law is merged into the text as if current while the record declares the markup preserved or absent (audit 2026-10-03). Awaiting a re-run with strike and underline recovery.

charCount.title: Charcount
charCount.description: Length of the law's full text in characters, the same as `totalChars` on the body. Null when there is no text. It is reported for a withheld law too (a fact about the text we hold), though that text is not served.

estimatedBodyPages.title: Estimatedbodypages
estimatedBodyPages.description: How many body pages the text takes: `charCount` divided by the page size (30,000 characters), rounded up. Pages are cut back to a paragraph break, so a long act can run a few percent over. Null unless `textStatus` is `held`: there is nothing to read. Reading a whole law costs `estimatedBodyPages` times the price of one body page (6 credits per page on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`). Ohio's 2025 budget act (HB 96) is 9,571,132 characters, about 320 pages or 1,920 credits to read in full; most acts are a page or two.

textSha256.title: Textsha256
textSha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the full text of this law. It changes only when the text does, so it is the cheap way to tell whether a copy you hold is current. Body pages carry the same value.

versionNo.title: Versionno
versionNo.description: Revision counter of our record of this law: 1 for the first collection, higher after a re-collection changed the text or the metadata. Not a legislative version.

amendatoryMarkup.title: Amendatorymarkup
amendatoryMarkup.description: Whether the language an amending act strikes and inserts survives in the text. `preserved`: it is in `text`, in the convention `markupConvention` names. `lost`: the publisher printed it and our text does not keep it, so deleted words can read as law: check the source before quoting. `absent`: the act carries no such markup that we found. `not_applicable`: there is no text to carry it.

markupConvention.title: Markupconvention
markupConvention.description: How preserved markup is written, set only when `amendatoryMarkup` is `preserved`. `wdiff`: deleted language is `[-like this-]` and inserted language `{+like this+}`. `publisher_literal`: the publisher's own words are left as printed (Minnesota prints `new text begin` / `new text end` and `deleted text begin` / `deleted text end` markers). `mixed`: both in one text.

documentKind.title: Documentkind
documentKind.description: What kind of document the text was taken from: `session_law_print` (the publisher's printed chapter), `enrolled_bill`, `slip_law`, `volume_extract` (carved out of a bound volume) or `other`. An open list. Null when there is no text.

identityConfidence.title: Identityconfidence
identityConfidence.description: How firmly the law's identity (session and number) is established. `single_source`: read from one publisher source, which is every state law at launch. `confirmed`: agreed by a second independent source, the level at which a `lawId` can be minted. `inferred`: derived by us rather than printed. `disputed`: sources disagree. The `sessionLawId` is the same at every level.

licenseNote.title: Licensenote
licenseNote.description: What the law's licence class is and what it means for reuse, in a plain sentence: `Government public: published by a government body with no restrictive terms, so the text may be reused, including commercially.` Every law served with text is of a class that permits reuse; a note saying otherwise describes a record whose text is held back. Free text to show, not an enum to branch on: branch on `textStatus`.
examples: Government public: published by a government body with no restrictive terms, so the text may be reused, including commercially.

updatedAt.title: Updatedat
updatedAt.description: When this law's record last changed in our registry, ISO 8601 UTC with a `+00:00` offset, the same form as the statutes routes. Use it with `updatedSince` on the list to sync only what changed.

citationAsPrinted.title: Citationasprinted
citationAsPrinted.description: The citation exactly as the publisher prints it. Null when none is printed.

vetoStatusAsPrinted.title: Vetostatusasprinted
vetoStatusAsPrinted.description: The publisher's own words on the governor's action. `enactmentOutcome` is our normalised reading of it.
examples: Signed by the governor March 17, 2025, 10:54 a.m.

pageCount.title: Pagecount
pageCount.description: Pages in the source document when it is a PDF. Null for HTML sources.

sourceUrl.title: Sourceurl
sourceUrl.description: The official page or file the act's text was collected from, on a government publisher's host: the first `sources` entry whose `role` is `text` and whose `hostClass` is `gov`. Open it to verify the text against the publisher. Null when we hold no such source (a law we know exists and have not collected) or when the text source is not a government host. Present on a withheld law too: the official copy is always where to go when we hold the text back.

effectiveDates.title: Effectivedates
effectiveDates.description: Every effective date the publisher prints for the act, in printed order. Always a list, never null; empty when none is held. Empty does NOT mean the act is not in force: a date printed as a rule (`the day following final enactment`) or not printed in the publisher's metadata is not guessed, and the approval date is never substituted for it. An act can take effect in parts, so a date may carry a `scopeAsPrinted`.

otherDates.title: Otherdates
otherDates.description: Every other date printed on the act, each with its `kind`: the approval date, filing dates and the publisher's own milestones (presentment to the governor).

codeSectionsAffected.title: Codesectionsaffected
codeSectionsAffected.description: The code sections the publisher's own table lists the act as affecting, as printed. Always a list. Empty when the publisher prints no such table, which is common: the title still names sections in prose. We do not read sections out of the act text into this list.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: The publisher documents the record was collected from, with the hash and fetch time of each: the audit trail from this response back to the official copy.

publisher.description: What the publisher itself printed or published about the act, beyond the dates and citation above: its own structured fields verbatim (`publisherFields`: the bill's action history, committees, sponsors, and vote counts where the publisher gives them), its own identifiers, the legislature number and the printed pages. Omitted, not null, when it cannot be read or we only know the act exists.

provenance.description: How we came by the text (the extraction method, the bound volume it was cut from) and the collector's own `caveats` on the record. Omitted, not null, when it cannot be read or we only know the act exists.

input.title: Input
input.description: The entry of your `ids` this law answers, exactly as you sent it (trimmed). When two entries name the same law, the law appears once, under the first.

status.title: Status
status.description: `resolved`: the law is in the registry and its text status is `held`, `withheld` or `pending`. `not_held`: the registry knows the law exists and we hold no text (`textStatus: not_held`); the record is still served, and charged like any other, because it is the answer the lookup was for.

body.title: Body
body.description: The first page of the law's text exactly as printed, present only when `includeBody` was true and the text is served. Null otherwise, and then not charged. Read `bodyHasMore` to know whether the act continues.
examples:
CHAPTER 1--S.F.No. 1552

An act

relating to agriculture; ...

bodyPageEnd.title: Bodypageend
bodyPageEnd.description: Character offset just past `body` in the full text: the first page starts at 0. Null when `body` is null.

bodyTotalChars.title: Bodytotalchars
bodyTotalChars.description: Length of the whole text in characters. Null when `body` is null.

bodyHasMore.title: Bodyhasmore
bodyHasMore.description: True when the text continues beyond `body`. Each further page is read, and charged, on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`. Null when `body` is null.

bodyNextCursor.title: Bodynextcursor
bodyNextCursor.description: Send as `cursor` to `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body` to read the next page of this law. Null on the last page, and when `body` is null.

SessionLawBatchLaw.title: SessionLawBatchLaw
SessionLawBatchLaw.description: One served law: the same record `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}` returns.

input.title: Input
input.description: The entry of your `ids`, exactly as you sent it (trimmed).

status.title: Status
status.description: `not_found`: no law carries this id (or it exists in another letter case, see `didYouMean`). `unparsed`: it reads as a citation and no state session law we hold carries it. `ambiguous`: the citation names several laws of one state, all in `didYouMean`, none chosen for you. `needs_jurisdiction`: the citation is in a form several states share and names none; `jurisdictions` lists where it exists. `session_not_fully_collected`: nothing matched and the session it points into is only partly collected, so the law may exist; `sessionCoverage` says how much we hold. `federal`: a federal act, served by `/us/statutes/section`. `error`: we failed to look this entry up; it is NOT a statement that the law does not exist, it is refunded in full, and it is safe to send again.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: The finer reason, the same vocabulary as `reason` on the 404 of `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`: `not_in_registry`, `wrong_case`, `unresolved_citation`, `ambiguous_citation`, `needs_jurisdiction`, `federal_session_law`, `missing_session_law_id`, `session_not_fully_collected`; or `lookup_failed` when `status` is `error`. Branch on `status`, which is the closed set; the wording of a reason can grow.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: A sentence safe to show a user, the same text the single route's 404 carries.
examples: Session law not found. No law in the registry carries this id. Take ids from a /us/session-laws/list result, or send the citation in its place.

didYouMean.title: Didyoumean
didYouMean.description: Real `sessionLawId`s the entry points at: the one that exists in another case, or every law an ambiguous citation names (at most 20, the conventional reading first). Empty when nothing matched.

defaultSessionLawId.title: Defaultsessionlawid
defaultSessionLawId.description: On `ambiguous`, the conventional reading when the registry records one. Informational: it is never served for you.

jurisdictions.title: Jurisdictions
jurisdictions.description: On `needs_jurisdiction`, every state (lower-case postal code) where the citation exists. Name one in the citation, or send `jurisdiction`, and resend. Null otherwise.

candidateCount.title: Candidatecount
candidateCount.description: On `ambiguous` and `needs_jurisdiction`, how many laws the citation names in all. When it exceeds `len(didYouMean)` the list is a sample. Null otherwise.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: True when `didYouMean` was capped and `candidateCount` is larger. Null otherwise.

sessionCoverage.description: On `session_not_fully_collected`, the partly collected session the entry points into: how many laws we hold of how many it should have. Null otherwise.

SessionLawBatchMiss.title: SessionLawBatchMiss
SessionLawBatchMiss.description: One entry of `ids` that did not yield a law, and why.

ids.title: Ids
ids.description: State session law ids, or citations, to read: up to 50 DISTINCT entries per call. Each entry is read exactly as the `{sessionLawId}` path of `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}` reads one: an id as sent, an id carrying copy damage, or a citation (`Minn. Laws 2025, ch. 1`, `P.A. 104-0001`, `S.F.No. 1552`). Entries are trimmed, and blank ones are dropped. Duplicates collapse FIRST (the first spelling wins, order is kept) and the cap applies to what is left, so a list quoting one law sixty times is one entry; `deduped` says how many were collapsed. 200 is the ceiling on the raw list. An entry is at most 300 characters. Federal ids (`SAL_...`) and endpoint names are misses, never charged.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Optional two-letter state code that scopes how a CITATION in `ids` is read, for the whole batch: it supplies the state a citation does not name (`Laws 2025, ch. 1` with `mn` is Minnesota's) and vetoes a state the citation does name or whose form belongs to another. Ignored for an id. The 50 states, `dc` and `pr`, case-insensitive; `federal` or an unknown code is a 422 and nothing is charged. Omit it for a batch whose citations each name their own state.

includeBody.title: Includebody
includeBody.description: Return the FIRST page of each served law's text inline, on `body`, beside the record. A page is about 30,000 characters and costs the ordinary body price (6 credits) per law whose page is served; a law whose text is withheld, not held or empty comes back with `body: null` and is not charged for it. Read `creditsConsumed` rather than computing the total: the worst case is 50 laws at 2 + 6 credits each. `bodyNextCursor` continues a longer act on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`.

laws.title: Laws
laws.description: The served laws, one per distinct law, in the order the entries of `ids` first reached them. Entries that missed are NOT here, so a client mapping by position must use `input` on each law (or `notFound`), never the index.

resolved.title: Resolved
resolved.description: One entry per input that did NOT match an id exactly as sent: a citation resolved to its law, or an id cleaned of whitespace, quotes or a trailing period. Includes an input whose law an earlier entry already produced, so every input is mappable onto `laws`. Empty when every entry was an exact id.

notFound.title: Notfound
notFound.description: Every entry that did not yield a law, in the order sent, each with its `status` and `reason`. A miss is not charged for the route's own price. An entry read as a CITATION also paid the resolve price, kept whenever we gave a verdict on it (`unparsed`, `ambiguous`, `needs_jurisdiction`, `federal`) and refunded on `session_not_fully_collected` and `error`. An id pays no resolve price.

deduped.title: Deduped
deduped.description: How many entries of `ids` were collapsed because an earlier entry was identical after trimming. Zero when none were. Two DIFFERENT spellings of one law are not counted here: the law appears once in `laws` and both spellings are in `resolved`.

creditsConsumed.title: Creditsconsumed
creditsConsumed.description: Credits actually charged for this call, never the list price: 2 per law served, plus the 2-credit resolve price for each citation whose resolution is kept, plus the body price per `body` served. Misses and failures bill nothing for the route.

processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems
processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Not billed on.

processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems
processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Not billed on.

creditsConsumed.title: Creditsconsumed
creditsConsumed.description: Credits actually charged for this call, never the list price. It includes the `/us/statutes/resolve` fee when a citation was sent where an id goes. 0 when the call was not charged or was refunded (a body that answers `available: false`).

sessionLawId.title: Sessionlawid
sessionLawId.description: The law this page belongs to.

citation.title: Citation
citation.description: The act's citation as its publisher prints it, the same as `citation` on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`. Carried here so a page is attributable on its own, with no second call.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Lowercase two-letter code of the state, `dc` or `pr`.

session.description: The legislative session the law was enacted in.

approvedDate.title: Approveddate
approvedDate.description: Date the governor approved the act, ISO 8601, as on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`: never an effective date. Null when none is held. See `approvedDateDerived`.

approvedDateDerived.title: Approveddatederived
approvedDateDerived.description: True only when `approvedDate` was filled from the publisher's dated signature label rather than held as the approval date. See the same field on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

sourceUrl.title: Sourceurl
sourceUrl.description: The official page or file this text was collected from, on a government publisher's host. Present on EVERY outcome, a withheld or not-held law included, so a reader is never at a dead end: where we do not serve the text, this is where to read it. Null only when we hold no government text source for the law.

available.title: Available
available.description: False when we do not serve this law's text; `reason` says why. A page with `available: false` is not charged.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why `available` is false: `not_held`, `withheld`, `pending` or `empty_text`. Null when the text is served.

textStatus.title: Textstatus
textStatus.description: Whether we serve this law's text. `held`: the text is served by `/us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`. `withheld`: we hold the text but a measured defect keeps it from being served, and `withheldReason` says what. `not_held`: we know the act exists and do not hold its text. `pending`: collected and not yet verified.

withheldReason.title: Withheldreason
withheldReason.description: Present only when `textStatus` is `withheld`: what is wrong with the text we hold. A plain sentence to show, not an enum to branch on.
examples: LA: struck (deleted) law is merged into the text as if current while the record declares the markup preserved or absent (audit 2026-10-03). Awaiting a re-run with strike and underline recovery.

text.title: Text
text.description: This page of the act's text, exactly as printed, in reading order. Concatenating every page's `text` in order reproduces the whole text. Where `amendatoryMarkup` is `preserved`, struck and inserted language is in the text in the convention `markupConvention` names. Null when `available` is false.
examples:
CHAPTER 1--S.F.No. 1552

An act

relating to agriculture; ...

pageStart.title: Pagestart
pageStart.description: Character offset in the full text where this page starts (0-based). Pages are contiguous: the next page's `pageStart` equals this page's `pageEnd`.

pageEnd.title: Pageend
pageEnd.description: Character offset just past this page. A page is about 30,000 characters, cut back to a paragraph break where one is near, so the length varies.

totalChars.title: Totalchars
totalChars.description: Length of the whole text in characters. This page is the last when `pageEnd` equals it.

totalPages.title: Totalpages
totalPages.description: Estimated pages in the whole text: `totalChars` divided by the page size, rounded up. Pages are cut back to a paragraph break, so a long act can run a few percent over. Null when no text is served.

pagePrice.title: Pageprice
pagePrice.description: Credits charged for the page in this response, the same as `creditsConsumed` on this route: the price of one page when a page was served, 0 when none was (`available` is false). Each further page costs the same.

estimatedRemainingCredits.title: Estimatedremainingcredits
estimatedRemainingCredits.description: Estimated credits to read the rest of the text from `pageEnd`: the pages still to come (`totalChars` less `pageEnd`, over the page size, rounded up) times the price of a page. 0 on the last page. Null when no text is served. An estimate: a page cut back to a paragraph break can add a page on a long act. Reading a whole law costs `estimatedBodyPages` times the price of one body page (6 credits per page on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`). Ohio's 2025 budget act (HB 96) is 9,571,132 characters, about 320 pages or 1,920 credits to read in full; most acts are a page or two.

textSha256.title: Textsha256
textSha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the full text of this law. It changes only when the text does, so it is the cheap way to tell whether a copy you hold is current. Body pages carry the same value.

amendatoryMarkup.title: Amendatorymarkup
amendatoryMarkup.description: Whether the language an amending act strikes and inserts survives in the text. `preserved`: it is in `text`, in the convention `markupConvention` names. `lost`: the publisher printed it and our text does not keep it, so deleted words can read as law: check the source before quoting. `absent`: the act carries no such markup that we found. `not_applicable`: there is no text to carry it.

markupConvention.title: Markupconvention
markupConvention.description: How preserved markup is written, set only when `amendatoryMarkup` is `preserved`. `wdiff`: deleted language is `[-like this-]` and inserted language `{+like this+}`. `publisher_literal`: the publisher's own words are left as printed (Minnesota prints `new text begin` / `new text end` and `deleted text begin` / `deleted text end` markers). `mixed`: both in one text.

nextCursor.title: Nextcursor
nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page: send it as `cursor` on the same path. Null on the last page. It is tied to this exact text, so a cursor from before the text was re-collected is a 409.

hasMore.title: Hasmore
hasMore.description: True when more pages follow; fetch them with `nextCursor`. Each page is charged.

id.title: Id
id.description: The entry's position in the feed: an integer that only ever grows. Send the largest `id` you hold as `sinceId` to read what came after it.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: What happened to the law. `added`: the registry learned the act exists. `text_available`: its text was collected. `corrected`: our reading of the law (its identity, dates or text) was corrected, so a copy you hold may be stale. `served`: it began to be served by this API. `unserved`: it stopped being served. `withdrawn`: it was removed from the registry, a tombstone: `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}` no longer answers it. `merged`: it was found to be the same law as another and merged into it, also a tombstone. So far every entry is `served`, one per law served when the registry went live; the other kinds appear as laws change. A consumer should treat a kind it does not know as `corrected`: re-read the law.

sessionLawId.title: Sessionlawid
sessionLawId.description: The law this entry is about. Read it at `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`, except after `withdrawn` or `merged`, when it no longer answers.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Lowercase two-letter code of the state, `dc` or `pr`.

detectedAt.title: Detectedat
detectedAt.description: When we recorded the change, ISO 8601 in UTC: the start of the transaction that wrote it. An upper bound on when the law changed in the world, never the date the law took effect or was approved.

SessionLawChange.title: SessionLawChange
SessionLawChange.description: One entry of the registry feed.

changes.title: Changes
changes.description: The entries after `sinceId`, oldest first, at most `limit`. Empty when nothing changed since your cursor, which is an answer and is charged.

cursor.title: Cursor
cursor.description: The largest `id` on this page: send it as `sinceId` for the next page. Null when the page is empty, so keep the cursor you already hold.

hasMore.title: Hasmore
hasMore.description: True when more entries follow this page: call again with `sinceId` set to `cursor` straight away. False means you have caught up as of this call.

creditsConsumed.title: Creditsconsumed
creditsConsumed.description: Credits actually charged for this call, never the list price. 0 when the call was refunded (a failure on our side).

processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems
processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Not billed on.

session.description: The session the law was enacted in.

textStatus.title: Textstatus
textStatus.description: `held`: the text is served. `withheld`: the law is listed but its text is withheld, see the law itself for why. `not_held` and `pending`: no text yet.

title.title: Title
title.description: The act's title, as the publisher prints it (usually `An act relating to ...`). Null when none is printed.
examples: An act relating to agriculture; modifying financial reporting requirements for grain buyers; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 223.17, subdivision 6.

billNumber.title: Billnumber
billNumber.description: The bill the act originated as, as the publisher prints it. Null when none is printed.

approvedDate.title: Approveddate
approvedDate.description: Date the governor (or the equivalent authority) approved the act, ISO 8601. Never an effective date. Null when none is printed.

effectiveFirst.title: Effectivefirst
effectiveFirst.description: Earliest of the act's effective dates we hold, ISO 8601. Null when we hold none: a date the publisher does not print, or prints as a relative rule, is not guessed. Read every date from `effectiveDates` on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

effectiveLast.title: Effectivelast
effectiveLast.description: Latest of the act's effective dates we hold, ISO 8601: equal to `effectiveFirst` when the act takes effect on one date. Null when we hold none.

enactmentOutcome.title: Enactmentoutcome
enactmentOutcome.description: How the measure became, or failed to become, law: `signed`, `became_law_without_signature`, `veto_overridden`, `line_item_veto` (signed with some items vetoed), `vetoed` and `pocket_veto` (not law), `not_presented`, `approved_by_voters`, or `unknown` when the publisher does not say.

sourceUrl.title: Sourceurl
sourceUrl.description: The government publisher's own URL for the act's text, so a citation answer links to the primary source. Null when we hold no text source from a government host.

href.title: Href
href.description: Where to read the law, relative to the API host.

isDefault.title: Isdefault
isDefault.description: True for the publisher's conventional reading of an ambiguous citation. Informational: no candidate is chosen for you.

SessionLawCitationCandidate.title: SessionLawCitationCandidate
SessionLawCitationCandidate.description: One session law a citation names.

status.title: Status
status.description: `matched`: the citation names exactly one session law, described by the fields beside this one. `ambiguous`: it names several, every one is in `candidates`, and none was chosen for you (Minnesota's 2025 regular and first special sessions each have a Chapter 1).

sessionLawId.title: Sessionlawid
sessionLawId.description: The law the citation names. Null when `status` is `ambiguous`.

citation.title: Citation
citation.description: Canonical citation for the act. Null when ambiguous.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Two-letter state code. Null when ambiguous.

session.description: The session the law was enacted in. Null when ambiguous.

textStatus.title: Textstatus
textStatus.description: `held` or `withheld`, as on the law itself. Null when ambiguous.

title.title: Title
title.description: The act's title, as the publisher prints it (usually `An act relating to ...`). Null when none is printed. Null when ambiguous.
examples: An act relating to agriculture; modifying financial reporting requirements for grain buyers; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 223.17, subdivision 6.

billNumber.title: Billnumber
