billNumber.description: The bill the act originated as, as the publisher prints it. Null when none is printed. Null when ambiguous.

approvedDate.title: Approveddate
approvedDate.description: Date the governor (or the equivalent authority) approved the act, ISO 8601. Never an effective date. Null when none is printed. Null when ambiguous.

effectiveFirst.title: Effectivefirst
effectiveFirst.description: Earliest of the act's effective dates we hold, ISO 8601. Null when we hold none: a date the publisher does not print, or prints as a relative rule, is not guessed. Read every date from `effectiveDates` on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`. Null when ambiguous.

effectiveLast.title: Effectivelast
effectiveLast.description: Latest of the act's effective dates we hold, ISO 8601: equal to `effectiveFirst` when the act takes effect on one date. Null when we hold none. Null when ambiguous.

enactmentOutcome.title: Enactmentoutcome
enactmentOutcome.description: How the measure became, or failed to become, law: `signed`, `became_law_without_signature`, `veto_overridden`, `line_item_veto` (signed with some items vetoed), `vetoed` and `pocket_veto` (not law), `not_presented`, `approved_by_voters`, or `unknown` when the publisher does not say. Null when ambiguous.

sourceUrl.title: Sourceurl
sourceUrl.description: The government publisher's own URL for the act's text, so a citation answer links to the primary source. Null when we hold no text source from a government host. Null when ambiguous.

href.title: Href
href.description: Where to read the law, relative to the API host. Null when ambiguous.

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description: Every law an ambiguous citation names. Empty when `status` is `matched`.

defaultSessionLawId.title: Defaultsessionlawid
defaultSessionLawId.description: On an ambiguous citation, the publisher's conventional reading when there is one. Never served for you.

SessionLawCitationMatch.title: SessionLawCitationMatch
SessionLawCitationMatch.description: A citation that names a STATE session law rather than a code section.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: What the date is, on `otherDates`: `approved`, `filed` or `other` (`kindAsPrinted` carries the publisher's label for `other`). Null on `effectiveDates`, where every entry is an effective date.

date.title: Date
date.description: The date as ISO 8601 when the printed text could be read as one. Null when the publisher's wording is not a calendar date.

dateAsPrinted.title: Dateasprinted
dateAsPrinted.description: The date exactly as the publisher wrote it, including any time of day.

kindAsPrinted.title: Kindasprinted
kindAsPrinted.description: The publisher's own label for what the date is, when it prints one.

scopeAsPrinted.title: Scopeasprinted
scopeAsPrinted.description: What the date applies to when it is not the whole act, as printed: an act can take effect in parts. Null when the date applies to the act as a whole.

SessionLawDate.title: SessionLawDate
SessionLawDate.description: One printed date on a session law.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: Where the total comes from. `stated_count`: the publisher states how many measures the session enacted. `complete_listing`: the publisher's own complete list of the session's acts, which we counted. `max_number`: the highest chapter number the publisher printed. `feed_total`: the total a publisher feed reports. `our_recount`: we counted the publisher's pages ourselves. `registry_union`: the measures we know of from several sources. `none`: no total is available, so completeness cannot be judged.

value.title: Value
value.description: The number of laws the session is expected to hold. Null when `kind` is `none`. Compare it with `registryCount` and `servedCount`.

derivation.title: Derivation
derivation.description: One plain sentence saying what `value` counts and where it comes from. Written for customers: it never contains our internal audit or collection notes.
examples: The publisher's complete listing of this session names 296 acts.

SessionLawDenominator.title: SessionLawDenominator
SessionLawDenominator.description: How many laws a session is supposed to hold, and where that number comes from.

code.title: Code
code.description: Session code, `{year}{type}{ordinal}`. `type` is `R` regular, `S` special, `X` extraordinary, `F` fiscal, `V` veto, `U` unknown. A regular session has no ordinal (`2025R`); a numbered special session carries it (`2025S1`, the first special session of 2025); a lettered one carries its letter (`2025SC`, Florida's Special Session C). `year` is the year the publisher numbers the session by, which for a period spanning two years is the first (District of Columbia Council Period 25 is `2023R`). Pass it as `session` to `GET /us/session-laws/list`.

label.title: Label
label.description: The session's canonical label, as the publisher names it.

year.title: Year
year.description: The year the session convened, the same year `code` starts with.

coverageStatus.title: Coveragestatus
coverageStatus.description: Whether we hold every law of this session. `complete`: every law the publisher lists for the session is accounted for, so a law absent from the list does not exist. `partial`: the collection of the session stopped short, so a law that is not found may exist, and this law's neighbours may be missing. The same verdict, with the counts behind it, is in the `sessionLaws` block on `GET /us/statutes/coverage`. Omitted when it cannot be read.

SessionLawDetailSession.title: SessionLawDetailSession
SessionLawDetailSession.description: The session block of a single law: the session, and whether we hold all of it.

denominator.derivation: The publisher's complete listing of this session names 296 measures. We hold 43 of them; the rest are not yet collected.

sessionCount.title: Sessioncount
sessionCount.description: Sessions of this jurisdiction we hold session laws for.

completeSessionCount.title: Completesessioncount
completeSessionCount.description: How many of those sessions are `complete`.

servedCount.title: Servedcount
servedCount.description: Laws served across every session listed.

series.title: Series
series.description: The numbering series that exist among this jurisdiction's session laws: the values `series` accepts on `GET /us/session-laws/list`. `general` is the ordinary chapter sequence. Omitted when it cannot be read, which is not the same as no series existing.

instrumentTypes.title: Instrumenttypes
instrumentTypes.description: The kinds of measure we hold for this jurisdiction: the values `instrumentType` accepts on `GET /us/session-laws/list`. Omitted when it cannot be read.

earliestApprovedDate.title: Earliestapproveddate
earliestApprovedDate.description: The earliest approval date among this jurisdiction's session laws, ISO 8601: the start of what the approval-date filters on `GET /us/session-laws/list` can match. Omitted when no law prints an approval date or the span cannot be read.

latestApprovedDate.title: Latestapproveddate
latestApprovedDate.description: The latest approval date among this jurisdiction's session laws, ISO 8601: the end of what the approval-date filters on `GET /us/session-laws/list` can match. Omitted when no law prints an approval date or the span cannot be read.

SessionLawJurisdictionCoverage.title: SessionLawJurisdictionCoverage
SessionLawJurisdictionCoverage.description: A jurisdiction's state session laws (acts as enacted), by session.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: `session` when the request named a `session`, `jurisdiction` when it named only the state.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Lowercase two-letter code of the state, `dc` or `pr`.

status.title: Status
status.description: `complete`: we hold every law the publisher lists for what you asked about, so an empty page means nothing matches your filters, and it is charged. `partial`: the collection stopped short, so the empty page may be a gap in our collection and not an absence of law; it is not charged when everything you asked about is partial. On a state-wide request (`scope: jurisdiction`) with some sessions complete and some partial the status is `partial`, `partialSessions` names the ones to doubt, and the page is charged, because for the complete sessions it is a true negative. `not_held`: we hold no session laws for this session or state at all (a state whose publisher we cannot yet collect from, for example); not charged.

session.description: The session you named, when `scope` is `session` and we hold any of it. Its counts are in the jurisdiction's `sessionLaws` block on `GET /us/statutes/coverage`.

sessionsHeld.title: Sessionsheld
sessionsHeld.description: How many sessions of this state we hold session laws for. 0 when `not_held`.

partialSessions.title: Partialsessions
partialSessions.description: Session codes of this state whose collection is `partial`: the ones an empty page may be missing laws from. Empty when none.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Present on `not_held`: why we hold nothing, in one plain sentence. A gap in our collection, not a statement that the state enacted no laws.
examples: Indiana publishes its session laws only through a service that needs an access token we do not hold yet.

message.title: Message
message.description: One sentence saying what this empty page means and whether it was charged. Free text to show, not an enum to branch on: branch on `status`.
examples: No law in this session matches your filters. We hold every law the publisher lists for 2025R, so this is not a gap in our collection.

SessionLawListCoverage.title: SessionLawListCoverage
SessionLawListCoverage.description: What we hold of the session or state an EMPTY page was asked about.

processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems
processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Not billed on.

creditsConsumed.title: Creditsconsumed
creditsConsumed.description: Credits actually charged for this call, never the list price. It includes the `/us/statutes/resolve` fee when a citation was sent where an id goes. 0 when the call was not charged or was refunded (a body that answers `available: false`).

results.title: Results
results.description: The page of laws, by `session.code` and then `sessionLawId`, both as text in the database's collation, not chapter order (so `..._C10` comes before `..._C2`; sort by `number` client-side if you need chapter order). The record without its dates list, sources or text: fetch those with `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

count.title: Count
count.description: Rows on this page. Never a total: the list is paged by cursor and has no corpus-wide count.

nextCursor.title: Nextcursor
nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page: send it as `cursor`, with the same filters. Null on the last page.

hasMore.title: Hasmore
hasMore.description: True when another page follows. Each page is charged, an empty one included, except an empty page that `coverage` reports as a gap in our collection.

coverage.description: Present only on an EMPTY page: what we hold of the session (or state) you asked about, so you can tell `nothing matches your filters` from `we have not collected this`. `status: complete` means the first: the page is charged. `partial` (the collection stopped short) and `not_held` (we hold nothing of it) mean the second: the page is NOT charged and `creditsConsumed` is 0. Omitted when the coverage cannot be read, in which case the empty page is charged as before.

detail.title: Detail
detail.description: Human-readable reason, safe to show a user. Branch on `reason`, not on this string: the wording can change.
examples: Session law not found. No law in the registry carries this id. Take ids from a /us/session-laws/list result, or send the citation in its place.

sessionLawId.title: Sessionlawid
sessionLawId.description: The identifier exactly as you sent it.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: `not_in_registry`: no law carries this id. `wrong_case`: it exists in another letter case, see `didYouMean`. `unresolved_citation`: you sent a citation and no law carries it. `ambiguous_citation`: the citation names several laws, all in `didYouMean`, none chosen for you; `defaultSessionLawId` is the publisher's conventional reading when one is recorded. `federal_session_law`: federal acts are served by /us/statutes/section. `missing_session_law_id`: the URL names an endpoint where the id goes. `needs_jurisdiction`: the citation is in a form several states share and names none, so none was chosen for you; `jurisdictions` lists the states where it exists and `didYouMean` one law per state. `session_not_fully_collected`: nothing matched, and the session the id or citation points into is only partly collected, so the law may exist; `sessionCoverage` says how much of the session we hold. The route's price is never charged on a 404; a citation's resolution fee is kept on `unresolved_citation`, `ambiguous_citation` and `needs_jurisdiction`, and refunded on `session_not_fully_collected`: a miss in a partly collected session is never charged.

didYouMean.title: Didyoumean
didYouMean.description: Real `sessionLawId`s the input points at: the one that exists in a different case, or every law an ambiguous citation names (at most 20, the conventional reading first). Empty when nothing matched.

defaultSessionLawId.title: Defaultsessionlawid
defaultSessionLawId.description: On `ambiguous_citation`, the conventional reading when the registry records one, otherwise null. Informational: it is never served for you.

jurisdictions.title: Jurisdictions
jurisdictions.description: On `needs_jurisdiction`, every state (lower-case postal code) where the citation you sent exists. Name one of them in the citation and send it again. Absent on every other reason.

candidateCount.title: Candidatecount
candidateCount.description: On `ambiguous_citation` and `needs_jurisdiction`, how many laws the citation names in all. Compare it with `len(didYouMean)`: when it is larger, `truncated` is true and the list is a sample, not the full set.

truncated.title: Truncated
truncated.description: True when `didYouMean` was capped (at most 20 ids) and `candidateCount` is larger than the list. Absent on reasons that carry no candidates.

sessionCoverage.description: On `session_not_fully_collected`, the partly collected session the id or citation points into: how many laws we hold of how many it is expected to have (`denominator`), and how many are still open. Absent on every other reason. The same block is in `sessionLaws.sessions` on `GET /us/statutes/coverage`.

textMethod.title: Textmethod
textMethod.description: How the text was extracted from the publisher's document: `pdf_text_layer`, `html`, `xml`, `docx`, `doc`, or `none` when no text was extracted. An open list. `none` is the same fact as `textStatus: not_held` for a collected law.

pagesWithText.title: Pageswithtext
pagesWithText.description: For a PDF, how many of its `pageCount` pages had a text layer to read. A figure below `pageCount` means some pages (a signature page, a scanned stamp) contributed no text. Null for a source that has no pages.

volume.description: Present only when the act's text was cut out of a bound volume of the session's laws rather than published on its own: the volume and the pages. Null otherwise.

caveats.title: Caveats
caveats.description: The collector's own remarks on this record, one string each, verbatim and in order. Most say something about the act or its text that a reader should know: where the chapter number came from when the act does not print one, that the publisher prints no strike-through so there is no amendatory markup to carry, that an effective date is the publisher's wording rather than a calendar date, that the text layer has kerning damage. Some are working notes about how the record was assembled and are published as written; they are free text for a person to read, not a vocabulary to branch on, and their wording can change. Notes that only describe how a page was fetched or decoded are not included. `[]` when there are none.
examples: Chapter number is from the publisher's Passed Legislation index ('Current Status'); the enrolled PDF prints a blank 'Chapter No. ____' field.
The 1-25 line-number column printed on every page is stripped.

SessionLawProvenance.title: SessionLawProvenance
SessionLawProvenance.description: How the text of an act was obtained, and what the collector noted about the record.

legislatureNumber.title: Legislaturenumber
legislatureNumber.description: The number of the legislature that enacted the act, as the publisher counts them (Minnesota's 94th Legislature, Alaska's 34th). Null where the publisher does not number its legislatures on the act's own pages; a gap in what we hold, not a fact about the act.

sessionLastYear.title: Sessionlastyear
sessionLastYear.description: The last calendar year of the session the act belongs to, for a session that spans two (the District of Columbia's Council Period 25 runs 2023 to 2024, California's regular session 2025 to 2026). Equal to `session.year` for a session inside one year.

printedPageStart.title: Printedpagestart
printedPageStart.description: The page number printed on the act's first page in the publisher's bound volume, as printed and therefore a string (`1`, `ix`, `42A`). Not the physical page of a PDF: see `provenance.volume`. Null where the act is not printed in a volume.

printedPageEnd.title: Printedpageend
printedPageEnd.description: The page number printed on the act's last page, as printed. Null as above.

documentKindAsPrinted.title: Documentkindasprinted
documentKindAsPrinted.description: The label the publisher's own document carries for what kind of text it is, exactly as printed: `Enrolled version` (Texas), `As Adopted`, `Pamphlet Law` (New Jersey), `As Enacted`, `slip copy of this session law`. Our normalised reading of it is `documentKind`. Null where the document prints none.

publisherIds.title: Publisherids
publisherIds.description: The identifiers the publisher itself gives the act, in the order it presents them: South Carolina's ratification number, California's `bill_id`, the District of Columbia's act and bill numbers, Maryland's `BillNumber`. Useful for joining to the publisher's own site or data. Which identifiers exist differs by state. Empty when the publisher exposes none.

otherCitations.title: Othercitations
otherCitations.description: Other citations the publisher prints for the same act, each exactly as printed: `Act No. 1` beside `CHAPTER 1`, `A.L.2025, c.1`, `70 DCR 1863`, `D.C. Act 25-5`. They are accepted as citations on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`. Empty when the publisher prints one form only.

publisherFields.title: Publisherfields
publisherFields.description: The publisher's own structured fields for this act, as the publisher states them and otherwise untouched: an object whose keys, nesting and values are the publisher's own words. The keys DIFFER BY STATE and are not normalised or renamed: Texas gives the bill's full action history with journal page numbers (`Actions`), Maryland the committees and the reading and hearing dates in each chamber, North Carolina and New Mexico a history that can carry vote counts, most states little more than the bill number and a sponsor. What a given state supplies is whatever its publisher printed; do not assume any key exists, and do not read a missing key as a fact about the act. Votes in particular are present only where a publisher printed them. A few values are the publisher's own HTML: treat every string as untrusted text and never render it unescaped. `{}` when the publisher printed no such fields. A value too large to serve is left out and its key named in `publisherFieldsOmitted`.

publisherFieldsOmitted.title: Publisherfieldsomitted
publisherFieldsOmitted.description: Keys of `publisherFields` that exist on the record but were too large to serve inline (past 64 KiB of JSON the largest values are left out, whole, never cut). Typically a publisher's full-bill HTML copy, whose text is on the body route in any case. Empty when nothing was left out, which is almost always.

SessionLawPublisher.title: SessionLawPublisher
SessionLawPublisher.description: What the publisher itself printed or published about an act, beyond the record's dates and citation.

name.title: Name
name.description: The publisher's own label for the identifier, exactly as it prints or exposes it, so it is not a vocabulary: `RAT#` (South Carolina), `bill_id` (California), `num type="act"` (District of Columbia), `BillNumber` (Maryland), `L.D.` (Maine).

value.title: Value
value.description: The identifier's value as the publisher gives it, always a string: `5`, `202520260SB26`, `25-5`, `HB0001`.

SessionLawPublisherId.title: SessionLawPublisherId
SessionLawPublisherId.description: An identifier the publisher itself gives an act.

input.title: Input
input.description: What you sent in the path, exactly.

sessionLawId.title: Sessionlawid
sessionLawId.description: The id it resolved to. Send this next time to skip resolution and its fee.

via.title: Via
via.description: `citation`: your input was a citation and matched exactly one law's citation form. `normalized_id`: your input was an id carrying surrounding whitespace, quotes or a trailing period, which were removed.

matchedForm.title: Matchedform
matchedForm.description: Which of the law's citation forms your input matched: `as_printed` (its printed citation), `bill` (its bill number) or `other_as_printed` (another printed form). Null for `normalized_id`.

SessionLawResolution.title: SessionLawResolution
SessionLawResolution.description: How a citation sent in place of a `sessionLawId` was matched.

processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems
processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Not billed on.

creditsConsumed.title: Creditsconsumed
creditsConsumed.description: Credits actually charged for this call, never the list price. It includes the `/us/statutes/resolve` fee when a citation was sent where an id goes. 0 when the call was not charged or was refunded (a body that answers `available: false`).

sessionLawId.title: Sessionlawid
sessionLawId.description: Permanent identifier of the law, the key to use everywhere. Shape `SSL_{state}_{session code}_{series}[_Y{numberingYear}]_{C<chapter>|B<billKey>}`. It never changes: a correction to our reading of a law keeps the old id working. Pass it to `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

lawId.title: Lawid
lawId.description: The law's identifier in the open us1 scheme. Null until its identity is confirmed by a second source and the us1 state shape is minted, so it is null on every state law today. Use `sessionLawId`, which is always present.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Lowercase two-letter code of the state, `dc` or `pr`. Federal acts are not served by this family: they are on `/us/statutes/section`.

citation.title: Citation
citation.description: The act's citation as its publisher prints it, falling back to `{session label}, ch. {number}` when none is printed. It is NOT unique: many states print a bare `CHAPTER 1` every session. Key on `sessionLawId`.

citableAs.title: Citableas
citableAs.description: The law cited the way a lawyer writes it, from the state's own form: `Minn. Laws 2025, ch. 1`, `2025 Fla. Laws ch. 3`, `Ill. Pub. Act 104-0001`, `S.L. 2025-12` (North Carolina), `Stats. 2025, ch. 12` (California), `Ohio S.B. 1 (2025)` for a state that numbers no chapters. A law in a special or extraordinary session carries it (`Minn. Laws 2025, 1st Spec. Sess., ch. 1`). Every value is read back through the grammar that `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}` accepts a citation in, and must name this law; one that would not is null, never guessed. Null where the state's form is not known, for a series with no standard form (resolutions, memorials), or for a law with neither a chapter nor a bill key. Where a regular and a special session each have a chapter 1, the bare form is the regular session's law and resolves with that law flagged as the default; the special session's carries its session. Distinct from `citation`, which is the publisher's printed form.

citationShort.title: Citationshort
citationShort.description: A compact label for tables and badges: `MN ch. 1 (2025)`, `IL P.A. 104-0001`, `OH S.B. 1 (2025)`. Not a form to send back: use `citableAs` or the `sessionLawId`. Null exactly when `citableAs` is null.

session.description: The legislative session the law was enacted in, and whether we hold all of it (`coverageStatus`).

series.title: Series
series.description: The numbering series the law belongs to within its session. Most states have one, `general`. Others number acts, resolutions or local laws separately (`public`, `act`, `acts`, `law`, `public_act`, `resolve`, `resolution_chapter`, `local`, ...). An open list that grows as jurisdictions load. Filter with `series` on the list.

instrumentType.title: Instrumenttype
instrumentType.description: What kind of measure this is: `act`, `joint_resolution`, `concurrent_resolution`, `resolution`, `resolve`, `memorial` or `other`. An open list. A resolution that was numbered and published among the session laws is included, with `isLaw` saying whether it binds as law.

number.title: Number
number.description: The chapter or act number exactly as printed, as a string. It is not always an integer: `1`, `2025-12` (Florida), `104-0001` (Illinois), `1A`. Null where the state does not number its acts (see `billKey`).

billKey.title: Billkey
billKey.description: Normalised bill identifier (chamber and type letters plus the number) that stands in for a chapter number in states that do not number their acts (Missouri, Ohio, Nebraska). `House Bill 2` is `HB2`. Null whenever `number` is set. Part of the `sessionLawId` as `B<billKey>`.

billNumber.title: Billnumber
billNumber.description: The bill the act originated as, as the publisher prints it. Matches as a citation on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

numberingYear.title: Numberingyear
numberingYear.description: The year of the numbering sequence the chapter number belongs to, where the state numbers by year (Minnesota, Florida, Texas). It appears in the `sessionLawId` as `_Y2025`. A chapter number is only unique within a session and numbering year: Minnesota's regular and first special sessions of 2025 each have a Chapter 1. Null where one sequence runs across the session (Louisiana).

title.title: Title
title.description: The act's long title as printed, usually beginning `An act relating to`. It names the code sections the act amends in prose.
examples: An act relating to agriculture; modifying financial reporting requirements for grain buyers; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 223.17, subdivision 6.

shortTitle.title: Shorttitle
shortTitle.description: The act's short title when the publisher gives one (Ohio, New York, the District of Columbia and a few others do), otherwise null.
examples: Enact Advance Ohio Higher Education Act

approvedDate.title: Approveddate
approvedDate.description: Date the governor (or the equivalent authority) approved the act, ISO 8601. Never an effective date: an act is usually in force on a different day, which is `effectiveDates`. Null when the publisher prints no approval date. Where the registry holds none but the publisher's own dated label on `otherDates` names the governor's signature, it is filled from that label and `approvedDateDerived` is true. The `approvedFrom` and `approvedTo` filters do NOT match a derived date: they read the registry's own approval date.

approvedDateDerived.title: Approveddatederived
approvedDateDerived.description: True only when `approvedDate` was not held as an approval date and we filled it from a dated label printed on the act (today South Dakota's `Signed by the Governor`, listed under `otherDates`), on an act whose `enactmentOutcome` is `signed` or `line_item_veto`. False when `approvedDate` is null or is the registry's own. We never read a `presented` or `passed` date as an approval, nor a signing label on an act that became law without signature.

effectiveFirst.title: Effectivefirst
effectiveFirst.description: Earliest of the act's effective dates we hold. Null when we hold none: a date the publisher does not print, or prints as a relative rule (`the day following final enactment`), is not guessed. The full list is `effectiveDates` on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

effectiveLast.title: Effectivelast
effectiveLast.description: Latest of the act's effective dates we hold. Equal to `effectiveFirst` for an act with one date; null when we hold none.

enactmentOutcome.title: Enactmentoutcome
enactmentOutcome.description: How the measure became, or failed to become, law. `signed`; `became_law_without_signature`; `veto_overridden`; `line_item_veto` (signed with some items vetoed); `vetoed` and `pocket_veto` (not law); `not_presented` (no governor action recorded, usual for resolutions); `approved_by_voters`; `unknown` (the publisher does not say).

isLaw.title: Islaw
isLaw.description: True for an act that is law. False for a numbered measure that is not: a vetoed bill, a pocket veto. Null when `enactmentOutcome` does not settle it (`not_presented`, `unknown`).

textStatus.title: Textstatus
textStatus.description: Whether we serve this law's text. `held`: the text is served by `/us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`. `withheld`: we hold the text but a measured defect keeps it from being served, and `withheldReason` says what. `not_held`: we know the act exists and do not hold its text. `pending`: collected and not yet verified.

withheldReason.title: Withheldreason
withheldReason.description: Present only when `textStatus` is `withheld`: a plain sentence saying what is wrong with the text we hold and what would release it. Free text, not an enum: show it, do not branch on it. The record itself (dates, sources, title) is still served and still correct.
examples: LA: struck (deleted) law is merged into the text as if current while the record declares the markup preserved or absent (audit 2026-10-03). Awaiting a re-run with strike and underline recovery.

charCount.title: Charcount
charCount.description: Length of the law's full text in characters, the same as `totalChars` on the body. Null when there is no text. It is reported for a withheld law too (a fact about the text we hold), though that text is not served.

estimatedBodyPages.title: Estimatedbodypages
estimatedBodyPages.description: How many body pages the text takes: `charCount` divided by the page size (30,000 characters), rounded up. Pages are cut back to a paragraph break, so a long act can run a few percent over. Null unless `textStatus` is `held`: there is nothing to read. Reading a whole law costs `estimatedBodyPages` times the price of one body page (6 credits per page on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`). Ohio's 2025 budget act (HB 96) is 9,571,132 characters, about 320 pages or 1,920 credits to read in full; most acts are a page or two.

textSha256.title: Textsha256
textSha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the full text of this law. It changes only when the text does, so it is the cheap way to tell whether a copy you hold is current. Body pages carry the same value.

versionNo.title: Versionno
versionNo.description: Revision counter of our record of this law: 1 for the first collection, higher after a re-collection changed the text or the metadata. Not a legislative version.

amendatoryMarkup.title: Amendatorymarkup
amendatoryMarkup.description: Whether the language an amending act strikes and inserts survives in the text. `preserved`: it is in `text`, in the convention `markupConvention` names. `lost`: the publisher printed it and our text does not keep it, so deleted words can read as law: check the source before quoting. `absent`: the act carries no such markup that we found. `not_applicable`: there is no text to carry it.

markupConvention.title: Markupconvention
markupConvention.description: How preserved markup is written, set only when `amendatoryMarkup` is `preserved`. `wdiff`: deleted language is `[-like this-]` and inserted language `{+like this+}`. `publisher_literal`: the publisher's own words are left as printed (Minnesota prints `new text begin` / `new text end` and `deleted text begin` / `deleted text end` markers). `mixed`: both in one text.

documentKind.title: Documentkind
documentKind.description: What kind of document the text was taken from: `session_law_print` (the publisher's printed chapter), `enrolled_bill`, `slip_law`, `volume_extract` (carved out of a bound volume) or `other`. An open list. Null when there is no text.

identityConfidence.title: Identityconfidence
identityConfidence.description: How firmly the law's identity (session and number) is established. `single_source`: read from one publisher source, which is every state law at launch. `confirmed`: agreed by a second independent source, the level at which a `lawId` can be minted. `inferred`: derived by us rather than printed. `disputed`: sources disagree. The `sessionLawId` is the same at every level.

licenseNote.title: Licensenote
licenseNote.description: What the law's licence class is and what it means for reuse, in a plain sentence: `Government public: published by a government body with no restrictive terms, so the text may be reused, including commercially.` Every law served with text is of a class that permits reuse; a note saying otherwise describes a record whose text is held back. Free text to show, not an enum to branch on: branch on `textStatus`.
examples: Government public: published by a government body with no restrictive terms, so the text may be reused, including commercially.

updatedAt.title: Updatedat
updatedAt.description: When this law's record last changed in our registry, ISO 8601 UTC with a `+00:00` offset, the same form as the statutes routes. Use it with `updatedSince` on the list to sync only what changed.

citationAsPrinted.title: Citationasprinted
citationAsPrinted.description: The citation exactly as the publisher prints it. Null when none is printed.

vetoStatusAsPrinted.title: Vetostatusasprinted
vetoStatusAsPrinted.description: The publisher's own words on the governor's action. `enactmentOutcome` is our normalised reading of it.
examples: Signed by the governor March 17, 2025, 10:54 a.m.

pageCount.title: Pagecount
pageCount.description: Pages in the source document when it is a PDF. Null for HTML sources.

sourceUrl.title: Sourceurl
sourceUrl.description: The official page or file the act's text was collected from, on a government publisher's host: the first `sources` entry whose `role` is `text` and whose `hostClass` is `gov`. Open it to verify the text against the publisher. Null when we hold no such source (a law we know exists and have not collected) or when the text source is not a government host. Present on a withheld law too: the official copy is always where to go when we hold the text back.

effectiveDates.title: Effectivedates
effectiveDates.description: Every effective date the publisher prints for the act, in printed order. Always a list, never null; empty when none is held. Empty does NOT mean the act is not in force: a date printed as a rule (`the day following final enactment`) or not printed in the publisher's metadata is not guessed, and the approval date is never substituted for it. An act can take effect in parts, so a date may carry a `scopeAsPrinted`.

otherDates.title: Otherdates
otherDates.description: Every other date printed on the act, each with its `kind`: the approval date, filing dates and the publisher's own milestones (presentment to the governor).

codeSectionsAffected.title: Codesectionsaffected
codeSectionsAffected.description: The code sections the publisher's own table lists the act as affecting, as printed. Always a list. Empty when the publisher prints no such table, which is common: the title still names sections in prose. We do not read sections out of the act text into this list.

sources.title: Sources
sources.description: The publisher documents the record was collected from, with the hash and fetch time of each: the audit trail from this response back to the official copy.

publisher.description: What the publisher itself printed or published about the act, beyond the dates and citation above: its own structured fields verbatim (`publisherFields`: the bill's action history, committees, sponsors, and vote counts where the publisher gives them), its own identifiers, the legislature number and the printed pages. Omitted, not null, when it cannot be read or we only know the act exists.

provenance.description: How we came by the text (the extraction method, the bound volume it was cut from) and the collector's own `caveats` on the record. Omitted, not null, when it cannot be read or we only know the act exists.

resolvedFrom.description: Present only when your input did not match an id as sent: it says what was matched and how. Null when you sent an exact id.

text.title: Text
text.description: The free words, quoted parts removed.

citationTokens.title: Citationtokens
citationTokens.description: Citation-shaped tokens found in the query (`63-3004`), matched exactly.

billNumbers.title: Billnumbers
billNumbers.description: Bill numbers found in the query (`S.F.No. 1552`), matched exactly.

SessionLawSearchParsed.title: SessionLawSearchParsed
SessionLawSearchParsed.description: How the query was read, so a caller can see why a result matched.

seq.title: Seq
seq.description: Position of this passage within the law, from 0.

ownStart.title: Ownstart
ownStart.description: Character offset in the law's stored text where this passage begins. Pass it as `startChar` to `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body` to read the law from here.

ownEnd.title: Ownend
ownEnd.description: Character offset where this passage ends, in the same scale as `ownStart`.

pageStart.title: Pagestart
pageStart.description: The printed page the passage starts on, 1-based, where the publisher's pages are known; else null.

heading.title: Heading
heading.description: The section heading the passage sits under (`Section 3.`), where one was found; else null.

snippet.title: Snippet
snippet.description: About 280 characters of the ENACTED text around your words, plain text, with `…` where it was cut. Language the act strikes out is never shown here.
examples: …the sheriff may establish procedures for using a credit card or debit card to make purchases…

highlights.title: Highlights
highlights.description: `[start, end]` character offsets INSIDE `snippet` (end exclusive) of each word that matched, so you can draw the highlight yourself. The snippet carries no markup.

bodyHref.title: Bodyhref
bodyHref.description: Where to read the text from this passage: the law's `/body` with `startChar` set.

SessionLawSearchPassage.title: SessionLawSearchPassage
SessionLawSearchPassage.description: The passage of the law that matched best, with a cut of its text.

query.title: Query
query.description: What to look for: a question in plain words (`can a sheriff pay with a debit card`), words from a title, a quoted phrase (`"credit card or debit card"`), a citation (`63-3004`), a code section or a bill number (`S.F.No. 1552`). Quoted parts must appear verbatim; everything else is matched on its words, stemmed, so `licensing` finds `licensed`. Words are matched as the legislature wrote them: `teeth cleaning professional` does not find an act that says `dental hygienist`. 2 to 300 characters.
examples: can the sheriff pay with a debit card

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Limit to one state, `dc` or `pr`. Two-letter code, case-insensitive. Omit to search every jurisdiction we hold. `federal` and an unknown code are a 422, never charged.

session.title: Session
session.description: Limit to one session, by the code `session.code` reports (`2025R`, `2025S1`). Case-sensitive. Matches the act's own session, so it narrows the TITLE, citation and bill signals; the passage text of an act carries its session year and type but not the code.

series.title: Series
series.description: Limit to these numbering series, one or more (they combine with OR). One of `general`, `public`, `public_act`, `special_act`, `private_and_special`, `act`, `acts`, `law`, `local`, `municipal`, `appropriation`, `resolve`, `resolves`, `resolution`, `resolution_chapter`, `joint_resolution`, `concurrent_resolution`, `memorial`, `initiated_bill`, `constitutional_amendment`. Any other value is a 422, never charged.

instrumentType.title: Instrumenttype
instrumentType.description: Limit to these kinds of measure, one or more (OR). One of `act`, `joint_resolution`, `concurrent_resolution`, `resolution`, `resolve`, `memorial`, `other`. Any other value is a 422, never charged.

approvedFrom.title: Approvedfrom
approvedFrom.description: Only laws approved on or after this date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive; a real calendar date (`2025-02-30` is a 422). A law with no printed approval date never matches.

approvedTo.title: Approvedto
approvedTo.description: Only laws approved on or before this date, `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive. An end before `approvedFrom` is a 422, never charged.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Laws per page, 1 to 25. A page costs the same however many laws it holds, so a larger `limit` is cheaper per law.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: Laws to skip, for the next page: `offset` plus `limit` can reach at most the 60 best matches. Each page is a new search and is charged. Deeper than 60 is a 422, never charged: narrow the search with a filter instead.

query.title: Query
query.description: The query as read, whitespace collapsed.
examples: can the sheriff pay with a debit card

parsed.description: How the query was split into words, phrases, citations and bill numbers.

results.title: Results
results.description: The laws, best first. Empty when nothing matched, which is an answer and is charged.

offset.title: Offset
offset.description: The `offset` this page was read from.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: The `limit` this page was read with.

hasMore.title: Hasmore
hasMore.description: True when more laws follow: call again with `offset` raised by `limit` (within the 60 best).

creditsConsumed.title: Creditsconsumed
creditsConsumed.description: Credits actually charged for this call, never the list price. 0 when the call was refunded.

processingTimeMs.title: Processingtimems
processingTimeMs.description: Server-side time for this request in milliseconds, excluding network transit. Not billed on.

sessionLawId.title: Sessionlawid
sessionLawId.description: The law's permanent id. Read the whole law at `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Lowercase two-letter code of the state, `dc` or `pr`.

session.title: Session
session.description: The session's code, as `session.code` reports it.

series.title: Series
series.description: The numbering series the law sits in.

instrumentType.title: Instrumenttype
instrumentType.description: The kind of measure: `act`, `joint_resolution` and so on.

citation.title: Citation
citation.description: The law's canonical citation, as the registry holds it.

title.title: Title
title.description: The act's title as the publisher prints it; null where the publisher printed none.
examples: Relating to Houston County; to authorize the sheriff to establish procedures for using a credit card.

approvedDate.title: Approveddate
approvedDate.description: The date the governor approved it, `YYYY-MM-DD`, where the publisher printed one; else null.

enactmentOutcome.title: Enactmentoutcome
enactmentOutcome.description: How it became law: `signed`, `became_law_without_signature`, `veto_overridden` and so on.

matchType.title: Matchtype
matchType.description: `exact` when a quoted phrase, a citation, a code section or a bill number you typed matched this law; `text` when it matched on words alone. It says HOW it matched and makes no claim that this is the right law: a question with no true answer still returns its closest words.

matchedBy.title: Matchedby
matchedBy.description: Every way this law matched, strongest context first. `title`: the words are in the act's title. `text`: they are in its enacted text. `phrase`: your quoted phrase appears verbatim. `citation`: a citation you typed (`63-3004`) appears in the text. `codeSection`: the act's own table lists that code section. `billNumber`: the act's bill number is the one you typed. A law matched by several ranks above one matched by a single way.

passage.description: The passage of the law's text that matched best, with a snippet. Null when this law matched only by title, citation, code section or bill number and no passage did.

code.title: Code
code.description: Session code, `{year}{type}{ordinal}`. `type` is `R` regular, `S` special, `X` extraordinary, `F` fiscal, `V` veto, `U` unknown. A regular session has no ordinal (`2025R`); a numbered special session carries it (`2025S1`, the first special session of 2025); a lettered one carries its letter (`2025SC`, Florida's Special Session C). `year` is the year the publisher numbers the session by, which for a period spanning two years is the first (District of Columbia Council Period 25 is `2023R`). Pass it as `session` to `GET /us/session-laws/list`.

label.title: Label
label.description: The session's canonical label, as the publisher names it.

year.title: Year
year.description: The year the session convened, the same year `code` starts with.

SessionLawSession.title: SessionLawSession
SessionLawSession.description: The legislative session a law was enacted in.

year.title: Year
year.description: The year the session convened, the year `code` starts with.

status.title: Status
status.description: `complete` when every law the publisher lists for the session is accounted for. Anything less is `partial`: a law missing from a partial session is not evidence that it does not exist, and asking for one by id or citation answers `session_not_fully_collected`, free of charge, rather than a plain not found.

servedCount.title: Servedcount
servedCount.description: Laws from this session we serve: every one we answer for by id, citation or list, whether or not we hold its text (`notHeldCount` of them have none). Laws whose text is withheld are not counted here, they are `withheldCount`. `servedCount + withheldCount` is `registryCount`, less any law still being verified.

withheldCount.title: Withheldcount
withheldCount.description: Laws from this session we hold and list but whose text is withheld for a measured defect (`textStatus: withheld`). They are real laws: their records are served, their text is not.

notHeldCount.title: Notheldcount
notHeldCount.description: Of the laws counted in `servedCount`, how many have no text held (`textStatus: not_held` or `pending`). A subset of `servedCount`, not an addition to it: do not add it to `servedCount` or `withheldCount`.

registryCount.title: Registrycount
registryCount.description: Every law of this session in our registry, whether or not its text is held: `servedCount + withheldCount`. Any difference is a law still being verified, which is neither.

collectedCount.title: Collectedcount
collectedCount.description: Laws from this session whose text we have collected, served or withheld. Compare it with `denominator.value` to see how much of the session we hold.

denominator.description: How many laws the session is expected to hold, and where that figure comes from. Null when it could not be read.

examples.derivation: The publisher's complete listing of this session names 296 measures. We hold 43 of them; the rest are not yet collected.

openGaps.title: Opengaps
openGaps.description: Laws the publisher lists for this session that we could not collect and have not yet. 0 on a `complete` session.

measuredAt.title: Measuredat
measuredAt.description: When this session's coverage was last measured, ISO 8601 UTC.

sourceIndex.title: Sourceindex
sourceIndex.description: Position of this source in the law's source list, starting at 0.

role.title: Role
role.description: What this document supplied: `text` (the act itself), `identity` (the publisher page that lists and numbers the session's laws), `metadata` (dates, veto and status tables), `code_sections` or `certified_image`.

url.title: Url
url.description: The publisher's URL for this document, as we fetched it.

fetchedAt.title: Fetchedat
fetchedAt.description: When we fetched the document, ISO 8601 UTC with a `+00:00` offset.

contentType.title: Contenttype
contentType.description: The document's media type as the publisher served it.

sha256.title: Sha256
sha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the exact bytes we fetched and archived.

byteLength.title: Bytelength
byteLength.description: Size of the fetched document in bytes.

hostClass.title: Hostclass
hostClass.description: `gov` when the document comes from a government publisher (including an official publisher on a non-`.gov` host), otherwise `other`.

SessionLawSource.title: SessionLawSource
SessionLawSource.description: A document the record was collected from.

sessionLawId.title: Sessionlawid
sessionLawId.description: Permanent identifier of the law, the key to use everywhere. Shape `SSL_{state}_{session code}_{series}[_Y{numberingYear}]_{C<chapter>|B<billKey>}`. It never changes: a correction to our reading of a law keeps the old id working. Pass it to `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

lawId.title: Lawid
lawId.description: The law's identifier in the open us1 scheme. Null until its identity is confirmed by a second source and the us1 state shape is minted, so it is null on every state law today. Use `sessionLawId`, which is always present.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: Lowercase two-letter code of the state, `dc` or `pr`. Federal acts are not served by this family: they are on `/us/statutes/section`.

citation.title: Citation
citation.description: The act's citation as its publisher prints it, falling back to `{session label}, ch. {number}` when none is printed. It is NOT unique: many states print a bare `CHAPTER 1` every session. Key on `sessionLawId`.

citableAs.title: Citableas
citableAs.description: The law cited the way a lawyer writes it, from the state's own form: `Minn. Laws 2025, ch. 1`, `2025 Fla. Laws ch. 3`, `Ill. Pub. Act 104-0001`, `S.L. 2025-12` (North Carolina), `Stats. 2025, ch. 12` (California), `Ohio S.B. 1 (2025)` for a state that numbers no chapters. A law in a special or extraordinary session carries it (`Minn. Laws 2025, 1st Spec. Sess., ch. 1`). Every value is read back through the grammar that `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}` accepts a citation in, and must name this law; one that would not is null, never guessed. Null where the state's form is not known, for a series with no standard form (resolutions, memorials), or for a law with neither a chapter nor a bill key. Where a regular and a special session each have a chapter 1, the bare form is the regular session's law and resolves with that law flagged as the default; the special session's carries its session. Distinct from `citation`, which is the publisher's printed form.

citationShort.title: Citationshort
citationShort.description: A compact label for tables and badges: `MN ch. 1 (2025)`, `IL P.A. 104-0001`, `OH S.B. 1 (2025)`. Not a form to send back: use `citableAs` or the `sessionLawId`. Null exactly when `citableAs` is null.

session.description: The legislative session the law was enacted in.

series.title: Series
series.description: The numbering series the law belongs to within its session. Most states have one, `general`. Others number acts, resolutions or local laws separately (`public`, `act`, `acts`, `law`, `public_act`, `resolve`, `resolution_chapter`, `local`, ...). An open list that grows as jurisdictions load. Filter with `series` on the list.

instrumentType.title: Instrumenttype
instrumentType.description: What kind of measure this is: `act`, `joint_resolution`, `concurrent_resolution`, `resolution`, `resolve`, `memorial` or `other`. An open list. A resolution that was numbered and published among the session laws is included, with `isLaw` saying whether it binds as law.

number.title: Number
number.description: The chapter or act number exactly as printed, as a string. It is not always an integer: `1`, `2025-12` (Florida), `104-0001` (Illinois), `1A`. Null where the state does not number its acts (see `billKey`).

billKey.title: Billkey
billKey.description: Normalised bill identifier (chamber and type letters plus the number) that stands in for a chapter number in states that do not number their acts (Missouri, Ohio, Nebraska). `House Bill 2` is `HB2`. Null whenever `number` is set. Part of the `sessionLawId` as `B<billKey>`.

billNumber.title: Billnumber
billNumber.description: The bill the act originated as, as the publisher prints it. Matches as a citation on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

numberingYear.title: Numberingyear
numberingYear.description: The year of the numbering sequence the chapter number belongs to, where the state numbers by year (Minnesota, Florida, Texas). It appears in the `sessionLawId` as `_Y2025`. A chapter number is only unique within a session and numbering year: Minnesota's regular and first special sessions of 2025 each have a Chapter 1. Null where one sequence runs across the session (Louisiana).

title.title: Title
title.description: The act's long title as printed, usually beginning `An act relating to`. It names the code sections the act amends in prose.
examples: An act relating to agriculture; modifying financial reporting requirements for grain buyers; amending Minnesota Statutes 2024, section 223.17, subdivision 6.

shortTitle.title: Shorttitle
shortTitle.description: The act's short title when the publisher gives one (Ohio, New York, the District of Columbia and a few others do), otherwise null.
examples: Enact Advance Ohio Higher Education Act

approvedDate.title: Approveddate
approvedDate.description: Date the governor (or the equivalent authority) approved the act, ISO 8601. Never an effective date: an act is usually in force on a different day, which is `effectiveDates`. Null when the publisher prints no approval date. Where the registry holds none but the publisher's own dated label on `otherDates` names the governor's signature, it is filled from that label and `approvedDateDerived` is true. The `approvedFrom` and `approvedTo` filters do NOT match a derived date: they read the registry's own approval date.

approvedDateDerived.title: Approveddatederived
approvedDateDerived.description: True only when `approvedDate` was not held as an approval date and we filled it from a dated label printed on the act (today South Dakota's `Signed by the Governor`, listed under `otherDates`), on an act whose `enactmentOutcome` is `signed` or `line_item_veto`. False when `approvedDate` is null or is the registry's own. We never read a `presented` or `passed` date as an approval, nor a signing label on an act that became law without signature.

effectiveFirst.title: Effectivefirst
effectiveFirst.description: Earliest of the act's effective dates we hold. Null when we hold none: a date the publisher does not print, or prints as a relative rule (`the day following final enactment`), is not guessed. The full list is `effectiveDates` on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}`.

effectiveLast.title: Effectivelast
effectiveLast.description: Latest of the act's effective dates we hold. Equal to `effectiveFirst` for an act with one date; null when we hold none.

enactmentOutcome.title: Enactmentoutcome
enactmentOutcome.description: How the measure became, or failed to become, law. `signed`; `became_law_without_signature`; `veto_overridden`; `line_item_veto` (signed with some items vetoed); `vetoed` and `pocket_veto` (not law); `not_presented` (no governor action recorded, usual for resolutions); `approved_by_voters`; `unknown` (the publisher does not say).

isLaw.title: Islaw
isLaw.description: True for an act that is law. False for a numbered measure that is not: a vetoed bill, a pocket veto. Null when `enactmentOutcome` does not settle it (`not_presented`, `unknown`).

textStatus.title: Textstatus
textStatus.description: Whether we serve this law's text. `held`: the text is served by `/us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`. `withheld`: we hold the text but a measured defect keeps it from being served, and `withheldReason` says what. `not_held`: we know the act exists and do not hold its text. `pending`: collected and not yet verified.

withheldReason.title: Withheldreason
withheldReason.description: Present only when `textStatus` is `withheld`: a plain sentence saying what is wrong with the text we hold and what would release it. Free text, not an enum: show it, do not branch on it. The record itself (dates, sources, title) is still served and still correct.
examples: LA: struck (deleted) law is merged into the text as if current while the record declares the markup preserved or absent (audit 2026-10-03). Awaiting a re-run with strike and underline recovery.

charCount.title: Charcount
charCount.description: Length of the law's full text in characters, the same as `totalChars` on the body. Null when there is no text. It is reported for a withheld law too (a fact about the text we hold), though that text is not served.

estimatedBodyPages.title: Estimatedbodypages
estimatedBodyPages.description: How many body pages the text takes: `charCount` divided by the page size (30,000 characters), rounded up. Pages are cut back to a paragraph break, so a long act can run a few percent over. Null unless `textStatus` is `held`: there is nothing to read. Reading a whole law costs `estimatedBodyPages` times the price of one body page (6 credits per page on `GET /us/session-laws/{sessionLawId}/body`). Ohio's 2025 budget act (HB 96) is 9,571,132 characters, about 320 pages or 1,920 credits to read in full; most acts are a page or two.

textSha256.title: Textsha256
textSha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the full text of this law. It changes only when the text does, so it is the cheap way to tell whether a copy you hold is current. Body pages carry the same value.

versionNo.title: Versionno
versionNo.description: Revision counter of our record of this law: 1 for the first collection, higher after a re-collection changed the text or the metadata. Not a legislative version.

amendatoryMarkup.title: Amendatorymarkup
amendatoryMarkup.description: Whether the language an amending act strikes and inserts survives in the text. `preserved`: it is in `text`, in the convention `markupConvention` names. `lost`: the publisher printed it and our text does not keep it, so deleted words can read as law: check the source before quoting. `absent`: the act carries no such markup that we found. `not_applicable`: there is no text to carry it.

markupConvention.title: Markupconvention
markupConvention.description: How preserved markup is written, set only when `amendatoryMarkup` is `preserved`. `wdiff`: deleted language is `[-like this-]` and inserted language `{+like this+}`. `publisher_literal`: the publisher's own words are left as printed (Minnesota prints `new text begin` / `new text end` and `deleted text begin` / `deleted text end` markers). `mixed`: both in one text.

documentKind.title: Documentkind
documentKind.description: What kind of document the text was taken from: `session_law_print` (the publisher's printed chapter), `enrolled_bill`, `slip_law`, `volume_extract` (carved out of a bound volume) or `other`. An open list. Null when there is no text.

identityConfidence.title: Identityconfidence
identityConfidence.description: How firmly the law's identity (session and number) is established. `single_source`: read from one publisher source, which is every state law at launch. `confirmed`: agreed by a second independent source, the level at which a `lawId` can be minted. `inferred`: derived by us rather than printed. `disputed`: sources disagree. The `sessionLawId` is the same at every level.

licenseNote.title: Licensenote
licenseNote.description: What the law's licence class is and what it means for reuse, in a plain sentence: `Government public: published by a government body with no restrictive terms, so the text may be reused, including commercially.` Every law served with text is of a class that permits reuse; a note saying otherwise describes a record whose text is held back. Free text to show, not an enum to branch on: branch on `textStatus`.
examples: Government public: published by a government body with no restrictive terms, so the text may be reused, including commercially.

updatedAt.title: Updatedat
updatedAt.description: When this law's record last changed in our registry, ISO 8601 UTC with a `+00:00` offset, the same form as the statutes routes. Use it with `updatedSince` on the list to sync only what changed.

SessionLawSummary.title: SessionLawSummary
SessionLawSummary.description: One session law, as it appears in lists and citation results.

url.title: Url
url.description: The publisher's URL of the whole volume (a PDF of every act of the session) that this act's text was cut from. A government host.

pageStart.title: Pagestart
pageStart.description: First physical page of the act in that volume, counted from 1 at the first page of the file. Not the page number printed on the page: see `publisher.printedPageStart` for that.

pageEnd.title: Pageend
pageEnd.description: Last physical page of the act in that volume, the same counting as `pageStart`.

boundaryHeading.title: Boundaryheading
boundaryHeading.description: The heading in the volume at which the act's text begins, which is how the cut was found. Null when none is recorded.

SessionLawVolume.title: SessionLawVolume
SessionLawVolume.description: The bound volume an act's text was cut out of.

actId.title: Actid
actId.description: The act_id of the section served. Equal to your request unless `resolvedFrom` is set, in which case it is the id your citation or cleaned-up input resolved to.

html.title: Html
html.description:
The section text as HTML. When `source` is `r2_render` this is our structured rendering of the publisher's source: real `` elements (with `
`, `colspan` and `rowspan`) and `

source.title: Source
source.description: Which copy the text came from: `r2_render` (our structured rendering, carrying `markdown`, `tables` and `figures`), `r2_s3` (the publisher's page for this section), `r2_text` (our per-section text extraction), `qdrant_reconstructed` (reassembled from indexed passages), and on `asOf` requests `stored_edition` or `corpus_change_history`. A storage identifier, not a citation: cite `sourceUrl`.

sourceUrl.title: Sourceurl
sourceUrl.description: Where this text was published by the government, so the bytes you were served can be cited and verified against the official record. Null when we hold no publishable link for the section: a third-party compiler is never served here, and an absent link is the correct answer in that case. `source` is a storage identifier and is NOT a citation.

content.title: Content
content.description:
The OPERATIVE TEXT of the section, with the source credit and the notes apparatus removed. This is the law; `plain` is the law plus everything the publisher prints around it.

Populated for **United States Code** sections, where GPO delimits the fields in the granule it publishes. Null for CFR and for state corpora, whose sources carry no equivalent structure -- null means "we cannot split this reliably", never "this section is empty", and `plain` is still the whole body.

Worth using if you feed sections to a model: the operative text is a median 46% of `plain` across USC and as little as 3.4% (`17 U.S.C. § 107`, where nearly all of the body is committee reports and amendment notes). A model handed the full body can quote a 1992 amendment note as the law in force.
examples: Notwithstanding the provisions of sections 106 and 106A, the fair use...

sourceCredit.title: Sourcecredit
sourceCredit.description:
The publisher's credit line for the section, e.g. `(Pub. L. 94-553, title I, §101, Oct. 19, 1976, 90 Stat. 2546; ...)`. Split out of the body rather than left inside it.

The same value is also on `GET /us/statutes/section/{actId}` as `sourceCredit`; it is repeated here so a caller fetching the text does not need a second call to know what enacted it.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description:
The notes apparatus the publisher prints after the section: Historical and Revision Notes, committee reports, Editorial Notes (codification and amendments), Statutory Notes and Related Subsidiaries (effective dates), and any guidelines reprinted by the editors.

Kept, not discarded: it is the legislative history, and it is the reason a section's body can be twenty times the length of the law. It is simply NOT the operative text, so it is served as its own field. Null where we cannot split the body.

Also null, deliberately, when you pass `format=operative`: that is the one format that asks us to leave the apparatus off the wire. Null there means "not sent", not "none exists" -- the same request at `format=content` returns it.
examples:
Historical and Revision Notes

house report no. 94–1476...

markdown.title: Markdown
markdown.description:
The body as GitHub-flavoured Markdown. When `source` is `r2_render` this is the structured rendering: tables as GFM pipe tables (a caption line above, footnotes below, multi-level headers joined as `Parent / Child`) and figures as `![alt](url)` at their position in the text. Returned only when `format` is `all` or `markdown`, not on the default `both`, where it would be a third full copy.

For a section with no structured rendering, `markdown` is null unless you pass `structured=true`, in which case it is the body as nested Markdown lists (the pre-existing behaviour). When both exist the structured rendering wins, because it is the one that keeps the tables; `subsections` is returned either way.

tables.title: Tables
tables.description: The tables in the body, in document order, with their size. An empty list means the section has none. Null means not known: the section's corpus has no structured rendering yet, so a table may still be present in `html`.

figures.title: Figures

hasFigures.title: Hasfigures

subsections.title: Subsections

asOf.description: Present only when the request passed `asOf`. Says WHICH version of the section you are holding and how far the evidence for it goes. Read `isBounded` before treating the text as the law on that date.

id.title: Id
id.description: Stable identifier for this change. Monotonic across the whole corpus, so it doubles as the paging cursor, and it is the id the board-watch diff endpoint takes.

changeKind.title: Changekind
changeKind.description: `added`: the section first appeared. `amended`: its text was replaced. `removed`: it disappeared from a full refresh of the source, which usually means repealed or renumbered. Note that a narrow, section-scoped refresh cannot observe a removal, so absence of a `removed` event is not proof a section still stands.

detectedAt.title: Detectedat
detectedAt.description: When our refresh OBSERVED the change, ISO-8601 UTC. An upper bound on the effective date, never the effective date itself: a source published weekly is seen up to a week late. Do not present it to an end user as when the law changed.

citation.title: Citation
citation.description: The section's citation as recorded at capture time. Null for corpora that do not carry one; `displayCitation` always has something readable.

displayCitation.title: Displaycitation
displayCitation.description: Always human-readable: the stored citation, or one derived from the section's hierarchy when the source recorded none. Use this for display and `citation` only when you specifically need what capture recorded.

hasDiff.title: Hasdiff
hasDiff.description: Whether the superseded text was captured, so a before/after diff can be rendered for this event. Always false for `added` (there is no before). Retrieving the diff itself needs a board watch covering this source: `GET /boards/watches/{watchId}/changes/{changeId}/diff`.

corpusType.title: Corpustype
corpusType.description: The board this change was captured on, e.g. `cfr`, `usc`, `state_regulation`. This is the value to subscribe to if you want alerts on future changes to this section.

state.title: State
state.description: Two-letter state code for state corpora, null for federal ones.

StatuteChangeEvent.title: StatuteChangeEvent
StatuteChangeEvent.description:
One time this section was added, amended, or removed by its publisher.

An OBSERVED change, not a publisher-declared one. It exists because a
refresh of the source corpus found this section's text different from the
copy we already held, so it carries the date WE detected it, which is at or
after the date the change took effect. For the publisher's own effective
and amendment dates, read `amendmentHistory` on the section itself.

actId.title: Actid
actId.description: The act_id of the section served. Equal to your request unless `resolvedFrom` is set, in which case it is the id your citation or cleaned-up input resolved to.

section.description: The section as it stands today. NULL is meaningful and not an error: it means the section is no longer in the corpus, which is exactly the case when the newest change is a `removed`. The history below is still the answer.

changes.title: Changes
changes.description: Observed changes, newest first by default. Empty is a real answer, and it means NO CAPTURED CHANGE, not that the section has never been amended. See `coverage`.

total.title: Total
total.description: Size of `changes` on this page, not a corpus-wide count: it is capped by `limit`.

hasMore.title: Hasmore
hasMore.description: True when the page filled to `limit`, so more may sit behind it. Page with `beforeId` (walking back) or `sinceId` (walking forward) rather than by raising `limit`.

cursor.title: Cursor
cursor.description: Highest `id` on this page, or null when the page is empty. Carry it into `sinceId` to poll for what is new; keep the one you hold when a page comes back empty.

observedFrom.title: Observedfrom
observedFrom.description:
The earliest change we ever captured for this section: the OBSERVATION HORIZON this history sits on. Read it before treating an empty or short list as the section's full history.

**Null means we have never captured a change for this section**, so an empty `changes` list is not evidence that it is stable. A non-null value with an empty list means your filters or cursor excluded everything we hold, which is a different answer.

`coverage` states the same caveat in prose. This is the fact behind it, and it is the same field, meaning the same thing, as `asOf.observedFrom` on `GET /section/{actId}/body`.

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: What this history can and cannot tell you, in one sentence. Change capture began well after the corpus itself did and is swept on a retention window, so this endpoint reports the changes we OBSERVED in that window, never the section's full legislative history. Read it before treating an empty list as 'unchanged'.
examples: Observed changes only, from when capture began for this source through today, retained 24 months. Not a full legislative history.

StatuteResolveBatchItem.title: StatuteResolveBatchItem
StatuteResolveBatchItem.description:
One citation's verdict inside a batch response.

Deliberately the same field names as `StatuteResolveResponse` minus the
per-request bookkeeping, so a caller migrating from the single route reads
each item with the code it already has.

citations.title: Citations
citations.description:
Bluebook citation strings to resolve. Duplicates are collapsed FIRST and order is preserved, so the response's `results` array lines up with the de-duplicated input.

The cap is **50 UNIQUE citations, applied after that collapse**, so a brief quoting one section sixty times is one citation and is accepted. 500 is the raw list ceiling, which exists so an unbounded list of duplicates cannot make us walk it.

Priced PER CITATION at the single-resolve rate, exactly like `POST /us/statutes/sections`: batching is a round-trip and latency win, not a discount. Thirty citations cost the same 60 credits either way and take one request instead of thirty.

state.title: State
state.description: Optional jurisdiction to resolve every citation WITHIN: a two-letter state code, or `federal` for the U.S. Code, the C.F.R., federal rules and the U.S. Constitution. Applies to the whole batch: a batch spanning jurisdictions should omit it and let each citation name its own. Same semantics as the single-citation route -- a constraint, not a hint.

corpusType.title: Corpustype
corpusType.description: Optional corpus to resolve every citation WITHIN: `STATE` (statutory text, federal or state), `REGULATION` (administrative codes), `STATE_RULES` (court rules), `CONSTITUTION` (constitutional text), `STATE_CONSTITUTION` (constitutional text; a synonym of `CONSTITUTION` here, since `state` is what separates the two). Same semantics as the single-citation route.

StatuteResolveBatchRequest.title: StatuteResolveBatchRequest
StatuteResolveBatchRequest.description:
Batch citation resolution. See `POST /us/statutes/resolve`.

`/resolve` took 1,159 calls in the 16 days to 2026-08-31, second only to
search, and every one of them carried a single citation. The caller shape it
is actually serving is an agent handed a brief, a memo or a model's output
with thirty citations in it, doing thirty round trips to check them.

results.title: Results
results.description: One entry per de-duplicated input citation, in the order supplied. An unresolved citation is an entry with `resolved: false`, never an omission: a caller checking thirty citations needs to know which of them failed, and a shorter array cannot say.

resolvedCount.title: Resolvedcount
resolvedCount.description: How many of the submitted citations resolved to a code section. A citation answered only by a `sessionLaw` block is not counted.

It is also set when the citation names a unit SMALLER than the one the publisher issues: Rhode Island cites a regulation by section ('250-RICR-120-05-15.2') but publishes the whole Part, so `section` is Part 15 and `subsection` is '15.2'. A non-null `subsection` always means `section` is the containing document, not the exact unit you cited.

Retry without the scope named in `excludedBy` to resolve it. No extra charge.

source.title: Source
source.description:
The named source within `corpusType`, for corpora that fold several independently filterable bodies of law into one token.

`FEDERAL_RULES` sources: `frcp` (Federal Rules of Civil Procedure), `frcrp` (Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure), `fre` (Federal Rules of Evidence), `frap` (Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure), `frbp` (Federal Rules of Bankruptcy Procedure), `sct` (Rules of the Supreme Court of the United States).

`CFR` sources: `far` (Federal Acquisition Regulation (48 C.F.R. ch. 1)), `dfars` (Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (48 C.F.R. ch. 2)) (both are already part of `CFR`; this only splits the existing Title 48 data by chapter, it does not add new sections).

`AGENCY_GUIDANCE` sources: `administrative_guidance` (Synthesized administrative guidance (e.g. SALT cap, CTC, 401(k) limits)), `ssa_ruling` (Social Security Administration Rulings), `irs_rev_proc` (IRS Revenue Procedures), `irs_notice` (IRS Notices), `irs_rev_rul` (IRS Revenue Rulings), `irs_announcement` (IRS Announcements), `irs_irm` (Internal Revenue Manual (IRS internal procedure)), `merger_guidelines` (DOJ & FTC Merger Guidelines (2023)), `doj_leniency` (DOJ Antitrust Division Leniency Policy), `doj_business_review` (DOJ Antitrust Division Business Review Letters (1991-2021)), `cms_iom` (CMS Medicare Internet-Only Manuals (instruction to Medicare contractors, not a regulation)), `copyright_circular` (US Copyright Office Circulars), `copyright_compendium` (Compendium of U.S. Copyright Office Practices, Third Edition (2014, 2017 and 2021 editions)), `doj_justice_manual` (DOJ Justice Manual), `uscis_policy_manual` (USCIS Policy Manual), `mpep` (USPTO Manual of Patent Examining Procedure (MPEP)), `tmep` (USPTO Trademark Manual of Examining Procedure (TMEP)), `cftc_staff_letter` (CFTC Staff Letters (no-action, exemptive, interpretative; 2008-present)), `fincen_ruling` (FinCEN Administrative Rulings), `fincen_guidance` (FinCEN Guidance (alerts, advisories, notices, bulletins, fact sheets)), `fincen_boi_faq` (FinCEN Beneficial Ownership Information FAQs), `fincen_boi_rule_qa` (FinCEN BOI Rulemaking Q&As (final rule and interim final rule)), `fincen_boi_compliance_guide` (FinCEN Small Entity Compliance Guide (Beneficial Ownership Information Reporting)), `fincen_amla_material` (FinCEN Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2020 Implementation Material), `frb_sr_letter` (Federal Reserve Supervision and Regulation (SR) / Consumer Affairs (CA) Letters), `occ_bulletin` (OCC Bulletins), `occ_interpretive_letter` (OCC Interpretive Letters), `fdic_fil` (FDIC Financial Institution Letters (FILs)), `cfpb_supervisory_guidance` (CFPB Supervisory Guidance), `cfpb_circular` (CFPB Consumer Financial Protection Circulars), `dfars_pgi` (DFARS PGI (Procedures, Guidance, and Information)), `ftc_advisory_opinion` (FTC Advisory Opinions), `ftc_policy_statement` (FTC Policy Statements (1967-present)), `ftc_hsr_interpretation` (FTC HSR Premerger Notification Interpretations: the Commission's formal interpretations under 16 C.F.R. 803.30 (1978-2000, a closed series) and the Premerger Notification Office's informal interpretations (1983-present; the publisher serves none from 1997)), `ftc_advocacy_filing` (FTC Advocacy Filings: comments and letters to state legislatures, state courts, governors and other federal agencies on the competition effects of a proposed measure (1985-present).
